name: ABAC input model: Subject/Action/Resource/Environment
description: Model the OPA decision input as four parts — Subject (who: id, roles, attributes), Action (what: a string verb), Resource (on what: type, id, attributes), Environment (circumstances: map). Keep this record framework-agnostic in opa-abac-core so the Spring modules and any client serialize the same shape as OPA 'input'. Pluggable extraction (JWT claims -> Subject) lives in the spring-security module, never in core.

content: OPA authorization helpers MUST fail closed: any error talking to OPA, any timeout, any unparseable response, or any ambiguity denies the request. Never default to allow on failure. The OPA client should treat a non-200 / connection error as 'deny' and surface it, not swallow it into 'true'.

name: Two-layer authorization: coarse gateway + fine app check
description: Split authorization into a coarse gateway layer (e.g. APISIX calling OPA to check the request maps to a known route + the subject holds the permission CATEGORY) and a fine application layer (the service runs an ABAC check on the concrete resource's attributes). The gateway is an explicit allow-list (default deny): every new endpoint path needs its own validator + allow rule, or it is rejected regardless of role. The app layer checks individual action permissions against the loaded resource. Both must agree; a new action needs updating in both places.

name: Hierarchical resource authorization (inherit from parent)
description: When resources form a tree (Catalog -> Category -> Product), a child can inherit authorization from its parent. Resolve the parent chain and let a grant on an ancestor satisfy a check on a descendant. Make this an explicit, opt-in 'hierarchical' mode on the authorization API rather than implicit, so callers know when ancestor grants apply.

Local APISIX container-pool rig (deploy.sh) failed to start in several non-obvious ways: (1) APISIX 3.x reads etcd config under deployment.etcd, not a top-level 'etcd:' key — a top-level key is silently ignored, APISIX falls back to 127.0.0.1:2379, logs 'all etcd nodes are unavailable', and the container exits. (2) bitnami/etcd images are gone (Bitnami sunset their free Docker Hub catalog) -> 'manifest unknown'. (3) Host port clashes with a running portal podman-machine gvproxy: :9080 and the 18081/18082 range are already bound. (4) Killing Postgres mid-session (e.g. compose down --remove-orphans on one of the shared-project compose files) makes pods return 503 with java.net.UnknownHostException: opa-abac-postgres.
resolution: (1) Put etcd under deployment.etcd in apisix/config.yaml. (2) Use quay.io/coreos/etcd:v3.5.x with explicit --listen-client-urls/--advertise-client-urls. (3) Use proxy port 9085 and pod base port 28080 (pods 28081+) to dodge the podman-machine. (4) All three composes share name: opa-abac-example so they share opa-abac-example_default; never run 'compose down --remove-orphans' on a single file — it deletes the others' containers. Pods auto-recover (HikariCP reconnect) within seconds once Postgres is back. Bonus: enable response-rewrite plugin and set X-Upstream-Addr=$upstream_addr on the route to prove round-robin.

name: Trace the APISIX->OPA->app->DB chain into Jaeger locally
description: Phase B of the example rig adds end-to-end distributed tracing. Pattern that worked: (1) Jaeger v2 + embedded Badger (jaegertracing/jaeger:2.17.0, --config=jaeger-config.yaml) for persistent traces with no JVM (avoids aarch64 SIGILL of ES/OpenSearch). (2) APISIX opentelemetry plugin via plugin_attr.opentelemetry.collector.address=jaeger:4318, enabled per-route with {"opentelemetry":{"sampler":{"name":"always_on"}}}. (3) OTEL Java agent BAKED INTO the app image (ADD opentelemetry-javaagent.jar /opt/otel/agent.jar) and attached per-pod via -javaagent + OTEL_SERVICE_NAME/OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://opa-abac-jaeger:4318/OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf. (4) OPA with distributed_tracing.type=grpc,address=jaeger:4317 emits its own decision spans. Verified: GET /api/services returns [apisix, catalog-management-service, opa, jaeger]; one APISIX trace nests gateway->app->JPA/DB spans. Note: APISIX opa plugin does NOT propagate trace context into the OPA call, so OPA spans are a separate service, not nested — expected. All host ports for Jaeger(16686/4317/4318)/OPA(8181) clash with a running portal podman-machine, so remap host side to 2xxxx; in-network DNS (opa-abac-jaeger:4318, opa:8181) is unaffected.

Wiring APISIX openid-connect to a Keycloak container hit two non-obvious failures: (1) 'unknown plugin [openid-connect]' on the route PUT — APISIX only loads plugins listed in config.yaml's top-level 'plugins:'; adding openid-connect there requires RECREATING the apisix container (editing the file isn't enough, and curl -sf swallows the 400 so the route silently lacks the plugin). (2) Keycloak issuer mismatch: Keycloak is hostname-aware, so the discovery doc + token issuer differ by how it's reached — in-network http://keycloak:8888 vs host http://localhost:28888. APISIX discovers + validates IN-NETWORK (issuer keycloak:8888), so a token minted against localhost:28888 has a mismatched issuer and is rejected. Tokens must be minted in-network or via the browser redirect flow.
resolution: (1) After changing config.yaml plugins, force-recreate apisix (docker compose up -d --force-recreate apisix) before seeding routes; don't trust curl -sf (drop -f or inspect the body). (2) Pin KC_HOSTNAME_URL=http://keycloak:8888 + KC_HOSTNAME_STRICT=false so the in-network issuer is stable; for testing, mint tokens in-network via 'docker run --network opa-abac-example_default curlimages/curl ... http://keycloak:8888/realms/catalog-demo/protocol/openid-connect/token'. Verified: no-token->302, valid in-network token->200, bad->401. ENABLE_OIDC gate keeps it opt-in. Service does NO JWT check (gateway-only auth, Phase 2).

name: APISIX gateway plugin ordering for auth chain (oidc->enrich->opa)
description: On an APISIX route that does OIDC + identity enrichment + OPA, plugin execution order matters and is controlled by _meta.priority (HIGHER runs first), not by JSON key order. Proven chain (matches portal): openid-connect(2599) -> serverless-pre-function enricher(2500) -> opa(2000) = authenticate, then inject identity headers from the validated JWT, then authorize. WITHOUT an explicit override, serverless-pre-function defaults to a very high priority and would run BEFORE openid-connect (no validated token yet) — so you MUST pin its _meta.priority below openid-connect. The enricher is a small Lua that base64url-decodes the JWT payload (already verified by openid-connect; it only READS claims) and sets X-User-Id (sub) / X-Username (preferred_username) via core.request.set_header. Build the Lua-in-JSON via a Python helper (json.dumps) to avoid bash escaping bugs. Keycloak omits 'sub' from the access token unless you add an oidc-sub-mapper protocolMapper to the client in the realm export (access.token.claim=true).

title: Gateway-side identity/enrichment is demo scaffold; the library does real extraction
rationale: The example rig's gateway does OIDC termination (APISIX openid-connect) and a Lua serverless-pre-function that decodes the JWT and injects X-User-Id/X-Username for OPA. This gateway-side identity handling is DELIBERATELY a throwaway demo so the topology is visible/traceable end-to-end NOW, before the library exists. It is NOT the target architecture. The project thesis (POC-ROADMAP) is to be Spring-NATIVE with no gateway 'mediator': real subject/attribute extraction belongs in the library — opa-abac-spring-security's pluggable Authentication->AbacContext extractor (see mx-ea7974), feeding OpaAuthorizationManager / @OpaPreAuthorize, with the service doing its own fine-grained ABAC (two-layer model mx-7130a1). So in Phase 3 the demo Lua enricher gets removed; the app validates the JWT and extracts AbacContext itself. Keep the gateway doing only coarse auth (authn + a coarse OPA route check); push fine-grained, attribute-level decisions into the app via the library. Don't let the demo enricher calcify into the design.

title: Base-entity layer: opa-abac-spring-data, plain UUID ids, tags on the secure base, mutate() as the safe write default
rationale: Foundational domain-model design for the clean-room starter (the DOMAIN-MODEL-FOUNDATION slice). Decisions: (1) the reusable base stack (AbstractAuditableEntity, AbstractSecuredEntity, ResourceTags + converter, LockableJpaRepository, AbstractCrudService) lives in opa-abac-spring-data — it already depends on opa-abac-core + spring-boot-starter-data-jpa, and opa-abac-core MUST stay Spring-free, so JPA/Spring annotations cannot live in core. (2) Trim typed-id value objects: use a plain UUID id. Our ABAC layer (AbacContext, AbacDataObject) is String/UUID-based and no planned feature consumes a typed id, so a wrapper is pure ceremony; reintroducible additively later. (3) Tags live ONLY on the SECURE base (AbstractSecuredEntity), never the plain one, and the secure base implements AbacDataObject so a secured entity is authorizable out of the box (the fix for 'secure = just a marker'). (4) JSONB tags via @JdbcTypeCode(SqlTypes.JSON) + an AttributeConverter (idiomatic on Hibernate 6.4) rather than a hand-rolled UserType. (5) Timestamps are OffsetDateTime + @TimeZoneStorage(NATIVE) -> timestamptz, matching the existing CatalogEntity.createdAt. (6) Concurrency: expose getById (unlocked) AND getByIdForUpdate (pessimistic) explicitly, and make mutate(id, fn) (lock+mutate+save) the safe-by-default write path — the generalized fix for inconsistent locking discipline that causes stale-@Version lost-update races. Verify serialization with a latch-forced concurrency IT on real Postgres (not H2). @AutoTag auto-tagging is deferred (tags set explicitly for now).

description: Spring Data JPA auditing (@CreatedDate/@LastModifiedDate) on an OffsetDateTime field throws 'Cannot convert unsupported date type java.time.LocalDateTime to java.time.OffsetDateTime' on save. The default auditing date source emits LocalDateTime and its DateConvertingAuditableBeanWrapper cannot target OffsetDateTime. Hit when the base entities standardized on OffsetDateTime/timestamptz.
resolution: Supply a DateTimeProvider bean returning Optional.of(OffsetDateTime.now()) and reference it via @EnableJpaAuditing(dateTimeProviderRef="..."). Auditing then uses the OffsetDateTime as-is, no conversion. (Same applies to any non-LocalDateTime audit timestamp type.)

description: Newman e2e chain broke: every request after 'create catalog' hit /catalogs// (empty id) and 404'd, even though the create step set the id via pm.collectionVariables.set('catalog_id', ...). Cause: the chained ids were ALSO declared (empty) in the Postman environment file. Newman resolves {{var}} with environment scope winning over collection scope, so the empty env value shadowed the captured collection value.
resolution: Keep runtime-captured chain ids in the COLLECTION scope only — do not declare catalog_id/category_id/product_id in the environment file. (Or capture them with pm.environment.set instead.) Also: in newman 6, an Auth/token request that run-tests.sh pre-injects can be cleanly skipped with a prerequest pm.execution.skipRequest() guard so it doesn't report a spurious failed request.

name: Generic pessimistic-lock repository fragment via SpEL #{#entityName}
description: One @NoRepositoryBean fragment serves every entity's 'select for update': @Lock(PESSIMISTIC_WRITE) @Query("SELECT e FROM #{#entityName} e WHERE e.id = :id") Optional<T> findByIdForUpdate(@Param("id") ID id). The SpEL #{#entityName} resolves per concrete repository, so there's no per-entity boilerplate. A concrete repo mixes it in alongside JpaRepository. A generic service guards getByIdForUpdate/mutate with 'instanceof LockableJpaRepository' and throws a clear UnsupportedOperationException if the fragment wasn't mixed in — opt-in and loud, never a silent unlocked read.

name: mutate(id, Consumer) as the safe-by-default write path
description: Make the correct-under-concurrency write the easy one: @Transactional MODEL mutate(ID id, Consumer<MODEL> fn) { var e = getByIdForUpdate(id); fn.accept(e); return repo.save(e); } — lock-for-update + apply + save in one tx, so two concurrent mutations of the same row serialize and neither sees a stale @Version. Callers write mutate(id, p -> { p.setX(...); }). Keep slow/external work OUT of fn (the lock is held until commit). Pessimistic mutate is the default; offer an optimistic mutateWithRetry only when blocking is too expensive. Prove serialization with a latch-forced IT on real Postgres (not H2): no StaleObjectStateException escapes, version increments exactly twice, both mutations applied.

title: Library-spine authorization is role-definition-driven, via a pluggable RoleDefinitionSupplier SPI
rationale: Generalizing the source platform's proven model: the OPA decision is driven primarily by the caller's role definition (code + attributes + permissions{resourceType:[verbs]}), with JWT tags as an override - NOT by raw token roles. Build RoleDefinition + RoleDefinitionSupplier as first-class core types NOW (with a NoOp default), ship a static DemoRoleDefinitionSupplier in the catalog app, and defer the HTTP-backed supplier (calling the user-management-service) to Phase 4 - a single-bean swap. This avoids reworking the OPA input / annotation / rego wire contract when the user-service lands, because the SPI isolates only the SOURCE of role definitions. Decided over (a) raw-roles-only now and (b) building the user-service first. Planned in docs/to-do/planning/LIBRARY-SPINE.

description: A custom AuthorizationManager<MethodInvocation> for a method annotation (e.g. @OpaPreAuthorize) read the annotation off invocation.getMethod(), which on a proxied bean is the INTERFACE method — so the method-level annotation on the concrete impl was never found and the manager abstained (returned null), silently letting every call through. Also a bare @EnableMethodSecurity context did not apply a hand-declared AuthorizationManagerBeforeMethodInterceptor @Bean to the target proxy, so the slice test never intercepted at all.
resolution: In the manager, resolve the most-specific method before reading the annotation: AopUtils.getMostSpecificMethod(invocation.getMethod(), targetClass) where targetClass = invocation.getThis().getClass(); read the annotation (and discover SpEL parameter names) off THAT method, falling back to the class-level annotation. In tests, drive the real AuthorizationManagerBeforeMethodInterceptor via ProxyFactory.addAdvisor(interceptor) (NOT addAdvice, which discards the interceptor's own @OpaPreAuthorize pointcut) so its pointcut gates the proxied method; allow runs, deny throws AccessDeniedException.

description: A Spring Boot starter registered its OPA-client JSON mapper as a top-level @Bean @ConditionalOnMissingBean ObjectMapper. Because the application's primary ObjectMapper was now 'already defined' by the starter, Spring Boot's JacksonAutoConfiguration backed off — so the app's MVC message converter used a bare ObjectMapper with NO JSR-310 module, and every response/error carrying an OffsetDateTime (audit createdAt, ApiError.timestamp) failed to serialize: 'Java 8 date/time type not supported by default'. Manifested as 500s / wrong status codes deep in integration tests, far from the cause.
resolution: A library/starter must NEVER expose a primary ObjectMapper bean. Inject ObjectProvider<ObjectMapper> and use objectMapper.getIfAvailable(ObjectMapper::new): reuse the app's fully-configured mapper when present (keeping JSR-310 etc.), fall back to a private one only when absent. Same rule for any extractor/serializer that needs a mapper.

description: A JWT->principal OncePerRequestFilter (AbacFilter) set the SecurityContext only when getAuthentication()==null. Installed via http.addFilterBefore(filter, AuthorizationFilter.class), it runs AFTER Spring Security's AnonymousAuthenticationFilter, which has already populated an AnonymousAuthenticationToken. So the guard saw a non-null auth, skipped, and every /api/** request was denied (403) by .authenticated().
resolution: Treat an AnonymousAuthenticationToken as 'not authenticated': attempt extraction when the current authentication is null OR an instanceof AnonymousAuthenticationToken; still never overwrite a real (non-anonymous) authentication. This lets the filter sit after AnonymousAuthenticationFilter and still take precedence.

name: Dual-token ABAC allow/deny e2e matrix through the gateway
description: To prove role-based ABAC end to end, run a Postman/newman matrix that mints TWO in-network Keycloak tokens (a viewer-only user and an editor user) and injects them as separate collection variables (viewer_token / editor_token), then asserts the matrix: editor seeds resources (201), viewer reads them (200), viewer writes are denied (403 via @OpaPreAuthorize -> role-definition-driven OPA), editor writes succeed (200/204). Crucial setup detail: the demo user must NOT hold both roles or it can't show viewer-denied-on-write — add a viewer-only realm user. Tokens are minted IN-NETWORK because APISIX validates the issuer as keycloak:8888; chained ids stay in COLLECTION scope (mx-ecc3ef). Keep per-request Authorization headers (Bearer {{viewer_token}} / {{editor_token}}) rather than a single collection-level bearer, so one collection exercises both principals.

title: App trusts the gateway for JWT signature; verifySignature reserved, not built
rationale: The app sits behind a validating gateway (APISIX openid-connect verifies the token against the realm JWKS before forwarding the Bearer), so the library's JwtClaimsSubjectExtractor does NOT re-verify the signature: it base64url-decodes the payload only and does structural + exp checks. This keeps opa-abac-core/-spring-security lean (no oauth2-resource-server, no nimbus/jjwt, no JWKS/key-rotation handling) and is the lean two-layer thesis (mx-7130a1). TRADEOFF, documented loudly: this is safe ONLY behind a validating gateway; deployed gateway-less / internet-exposed it is a vulnerability. A verifySignature=true property is RESERVED (a forward-looking config key) but deliberately UNIMPLEMENTED in this slice — the escape hatch for a gateway-less deployment. Verified end to end: a token with a garbage signature still extracts (the unit test asserts this), and the e2e matrix runs behind APISIX. Do not bolt signature verification on without also reconsidering whether the gateway should remain the trust anchor.

content: A security starter must NOT register its own SecurityFilterChain — it exposes beans and the application owns the chain. The opa-abac starter wires OpaClient/RoleDefinitionSupplier/AbacSubjectExtractor/AbacFilter/@OpaPreAuthorize-advisor as @ConditionalOnMissingBean, with the security beans additionally @ConditionalOnClass({SecurityFilterChain, OncePerRequestFilter}) (string-name form, isolated in an imported config so the types never load in a non-web app). The application declares @EnableWebSecurity @EnableMethodSecurity, builds its own SecurityFilterChain, and installs the injected AbacFilter (.addFilterBefore(abacFilter, AuthorizationFilter.class)). Inject AbacFilter via ObjectProvider so a permissive test profile (opa.abac.enabled=false) without the filter still builds a chain. Also disable Boot's auto-registration of the filter as a top-level servlet filter (a disabled FilterRegistrationBean) so it runs ONLY inside the security chain. Asserted in ApplicationContextRunner: doesNotHaveBean(SecurityFilterChain) when the starter is on.

name: Team-based resource access models across cloud platforms (AWS/Heroku/GitHub/GCP/K8s/OpenFGA)
description: Cross-platform study for designing a team-scoped ABAC-over-OPA model (creator->auto-owner->team->team-scoped roles->resource grant). KEY DISTINCTION every platform makes: role != grant/binding. A ROLE (GCP role, K8s ClusterRole, GitHub repo role) is a reusable named permission set; a GRANT/BINDING is {principal + role + scoped resource}. GCP names it cleanly: binding = principal + role + (resource) + optional condition. MODELS: AWS=account owns the resource (not the user); within-account access is the UNION of identity-based + resource-based policies, cross-account needs BOTH (two-key). Heroku=3 fixed team roles (admin/member/collaborator) + per-app view/deploy/operate/manage grants (coarse role + fine per-resource grant). GitHub=team GRANTS repo access (read/triage/write/maintain/admin); nested teams inherit parent access; join team -> inherit its repo perms; transfer-ownership makes new owner admin + old owner collaborator; orphaned repo needs Support. GCP=binding on a resource node, role inherited additively DOWN org->folder->project->resource; custom roles only at project/org (not folder). K8s=Role(namespaced) vs ClusterRole(global), RoleBinding can reference a ClusterRole to REUSE a global definition but SCOPE it to one namespace ('definition global, binding scoped'); anti-escalation rule: you cannot create a role/binding granting MORE than you already hold unless you have explicit escalate/bind. OpenFGA/Zanzibar(ReBAC)=tuples (user,relation,object); 'team is editor of folder' is the userset tuple (team:X#member, editor, folder:Y) -> every member auto-inherits; 'team grants access' is LITERALLY a userset. SYNTHESIS for our model: (1) owner-on-create = atomically write (creator,owner,resource) in the same tx as resource creation + keep a team-admin fallback so a resource is never grant-less; (2) prefer resource->team INDIRECTION over direct ownership (O(1) revocation, central audit, no orphaning) with an owner ROLE held by a person on top + first-class transfer-ownership; (3) ship immutable system roles (owner/administrator/member[/viewer]) for the common case, team-scoped CUSTOM role defs as gated opt-in; (4) authorize HYBRID in Rego: RBAC role->perms map in data, ReBAC-style join (subject member-of team AND team has-role-on resource) for 'team grants access', ABAC predicate owner==subject for bootstrap; OPA expresses all three over input+data. PITFALLS: self-escalation (use the K8s subset rule), confused deputy (authorize the ACTOR of a grant not the service identity), role explosion (keep roles reusable, scope via bindings, use ReBAC indirection not per-relationship roles), revocation propagation (membership = single source of truth so checks re-derive; invalidate caches on membership change). Full cited report + URLs lives in the USER-MANAGEMENT-SERVICE planning notes.

title: Team access is app-resolved first (HTTP RoleDefinitionSupplier); ReBAC-in-Rego deferred
rationale: For the user-management-service (Phase 4 team abstraction), authorization is APP-RESOLVED: the user-service owns teams + role definitions + grants (TeamMembership = the binding) and exposes an internal GET /effective-role?userId&resourceType&resourceId that walks user->memberships->team(matching team-target)->bound RoleDefinition server-side. The catalog app's HTTP-backed RoleDefinitionSupplier (app code, NOT a library change) calls it and returns a core.RoleDefinition; the catalog still passes role_definition in the OPA input exactly as Phase 3 did. Chosen over (a) token-claim delivery (token-size/freshness bound, pushes authority into Keycloak) and (b) ReBAC-in-Rego (push the team/membership/grant graph into OPA data and do the 'member-of team AND team has-role-on resource' Zanzibar userset join in the policy). ReBAC is the more elegant end state and the strongest portfolio piece but a bigger lift + different data-distribution model, so it is DEFERRED to a new Phase 7 where it can be compared against the app-resolved path. Key reason app-resolved ships first: it reuses the Phase-3 spine with ZERO wire change (the RoleDefinitionSupplier SPI already returns a RoleDefinition) and is a single-bean swap of the demo supplier. The model encodes role != grant (separate RoleDefinition + TeamMembership), fixed system roles (owner/administrator/member/viewer) + team-scoped custom roles, owner-on-create (atomic), transfer-ownership, the Kubernetes no-self-escalation subset rule, revocation-via-membership, and authorize-the-actor. The user-service dogfoods the starter by securing its own management API with @OpaPreAuthorize. Planned in docs/to-do/planning/USER-MANAGEMENT-SERVICE.

title: user-management-service is layered (dedicated service/) where the catalog stays flat; hand-written mapper, no MapStruct, no facade
rationale: Phase-4 user-management-service internal structure, decided with the maintainer. The catalog app is deliberately FLAT (config/domain/web; controllers call repositories directly; the only service, ProductService, exists solely for the optimistic-lock concurrency demo) to teach 'no ceremony needed to use the starter'. The user-service makes exactly ONE justified divergence: a dedicated @Transactional service/ package (TeamService, RoleDefinitionService, MembershipService, EffectiveRoleResolver). Rationale: its core operations are inherently CROSS-ENTITY and TRANSACTIONAL — owner-on-create (Team + owner TeamMembership in one tx), transfer-ownership (atomic up/down), the no-self-escalation subset rule (read actor effective role -> validate target -> write), and effective-role resolution (the membership walk). These cannot live in a controller without becoming a design smell; the catalog had none of these, so flat was right there. DECIDED AGAINST: (a) MapStruct — keep a hand-written static UserMgmtMapper mirroring the catalog CatalogMapper, for sibling-consistency in a repo meant to be READ, to avoid a third codegen stage alongside the OpenAPI generator, and because ~4 flat DTOs do not earn MapStruct nesting/bulk-copy strengths; (b) a facade layer — correct overkill for a single multi-aggregate read (effective-role resolution); the service/ layer IS that orchestration point, so a facade would be pure-delegation lasagna. Keep the service clean so a facade is a trivial LATER insertion if Phase 5 brings read-side orchestration (batch eval / list filtering). Principle: build the seam, not the layer. Net: user-service = config/domain/SERVICE/web — exactly one new package vs the catalog, every addition earned by the domain.

content: The example rig (Docker) is designed to run SIMULTANEOUSLY with the maintainer's proprietary portal stack (podman-machine) — do NOT stop podman. They coexist because the rig deliberately publishes every host port in a SHIFTED range so nothing collides with the podman portal: gateway 9085 (not 9080), catalog pods 28081/28082 (BASE_PORT 28080, not the portal 18080 range), OPA 28181 (not 8181), Keycloak 28888 (not 8888), Jaeger 26686/24317/24318, Postgres 5433 (not 5432); APISIX admin 9180. In-network DNS (opa:8181, keycloak:8888, opa-abac-jaeger:4318) is unaffected by the host remap. Both engines coexist as separate VMs/daemons; the ONLY shared constraint is host ports (resolved by the shift) and machine RAM/CPU (lever is --pods, not engine interference). OPERATIONAL ORDERING GOTCHA: deploy.sh does NOT start the base Postgres — it asserts 'opa-abac-postgres' already exists and ERRORS with 'Postgres not running. Start base infra first: ./profile.sh up' otherwise. So the correct bring-up is: (1) ./profile.sh up (base Postgres on 5433, healthy), then (2) [ENABLE_OIDC=1] ./deploy.sh up --pods N (Jaeger/OPA/Keycloak/APISIX/etcd + N catalog pods; OIDC is OFF by default — set ENABLE_OIDC=1 to exercise Keycloak token minting + gateway auth; OPA + tracing are on by default). Expected-correct signals: GET :9085/actuator/health returns 302 (APISIX openid-connect redirecting to Keycloak — that's auth working, NOT a failure) — verify the app itself via a direct pod hit :28081/actuator/health => {status:UP}. The 'Found orphan containers [opa-abac-postgres]' compose warnings are harmless (Postgres belongs to the profile.sh project, the rest to the deploy.sh project).

name: Team/role-def core: role≠grant entities, JSONB permissions, partial-unique role codes
description: user-management-service Phase-4 core domain. Four entities: User (principal, AbstractAuditableEntity, no tags), Team (AbstractSecuredEntity -> resource type 'team', carries team-target type+id with a unique constraint on (target_type,target_id) for resource->team indirection), RoleDefinitionEntity (the ROLE half; JSONB attributes + permissions in the {resourceType:[verbs]} shape the OPA policy reads; system flag + nullable teamId), TeamMembership (the GRANT half; unique (team_id,user_id), carries roleDefinitionId). Keep RoleDefinitionEntity named distinctly from the library's core.RoleDefinition record (decision/wire shape) to avoid a clash. System roles seeded by Liquibase with STABLE ids+codes mirrored in a SystemRoles constants class so app code resolves them without a query. System-role permissions use a wildcard '*' resource type (team-target-type-agnostic); the effective-role resolver expands '*' to the concrete team-target type. Role-code uniqueness needs TWO partial unique indexes in Postgres (CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... WHERE team_id IS NULL for system roles vs WHERE team_id IS NOT NULL on (team_id,code) for custom) — authored via a Liquibase <sql splitStatements:true> block, not addUniqueConstraint.

Testing the dogfooded @OpaPreAuthorize path over a RANDOM_PORT TestRestTemplate: a test config that set the 'acting subject' via a ThreadLocal (AbacSubjectExtractor reads it) silently authenticated NOTHING — the in-process server runs the request on a Tomcat worker thread, not the JUnit test thread, so the ThreadLocal set in the test was invisible to the extractor. Symptom: deny-path tests pass (member/viewer 403) but allow-path tests fail (owner/admin get 403 too), because the subject was always empty -> fail-closed deny. Also hit a second wall: providing BOTH the app's production SecurityConfig chain AND a permissive test SecurityFilterChain throws 'a filter chain that matches any request has already been configured' (Spring Security 6.4 forbids two /** chains). And a FilterRegistrationBean<AbacFilter> with a null filter (when the starter is off and no AbacFilter bean exists) makes Tomcat throw 'Filter must not be null'.
resolution: Pass the acting identity IN THE REQUEST (a header the test AbacSubjectExtractor reads), never a ThreadLocal, so it travels with the HTTP call across threads. Use ONE security chain everywhere (the real SecurityConfig) and drive test permissiveness through @Primary test beans (the subject extractor + an in-process OpaClient that mirrors the rego) rather than a second filter chain. Guard the app's FilterRegistrationBean<AbacFilter> with @ConditionalOnBean(AbacFilter.class) so it is never created with a null filter when the starter is disabled.

name: App-resolved effective-role: one resolver, two projections, pluggable team-target matcher
description: The user-management-service resolves a caller's effective role from LIVE team membership (membership is the single source of truth — always re-derive, never denormalize, so removing a member revokes immediately). One EffectiveRoleService is the single seam, returning TWO projections of the same membership: (1) a MANAGEMENT role (permissions['team'] = a capability ladder owner>admin>member/viewer) consumed by the service's OWN dogfooded @OpaPreAuthorize when securing the management API; (2) a RESOURCE role (the bound role's stored permissions, with a wildcard '*' resource type expanded to the concrete team-target type) returned by the INTERNAL GET /internal/effective-role?userId&resourceType&resourceId endpoint that the catalog's HttpRoleDefinitionSupplier consumes. The resolve endpoint is internal-only (permitAll under /internal/**, never gateway-fronted — an in-network attribute source), returns the raw core.RoleDefinition wire shape (code/attributes/permissions) so the catalog deserializes directly, and answers 204 (empty, NOT an error) on no-match so the catalog supplier maps it to Optional.empty() and the policy default-denies (fail-closed). Resource->team matching is a pluggable TeamTargetMatcher SPI (ExactTeamTargetMatcher default = exact (type,id) match; a hierarchy-walking matcher is an additive Phase-5 swap). The 'userId' param is the IdP subject (sub) the catalog forwards, not the internal user UUID.

name: Second service in the local rig + runtime-bootstrap e2e for app-resolved roles
description: Adding a SECOND example service (user-management) to the deploy.sh container-pool rig: a focused infra/compose.usermgmt.yaml (the service + its OWN Postgres on a fresh host port) added under an ENABLE_USER_SERVICE toggle that also flips the catalog pods to CATALOG_ROLE_SOURCE=http + the in-network base URL (http://usermgmt:8080). The user-service dogfoods the starter, so its team.rego must be COPIED into the shared OPA's mounted policy dir (infra/opa/policies/) — the service's own resources/opa/policies/ is the source of truth; restart OPA after editing (--watch doesn't always reload, mx-4e1191). The e2e challenge: the team-target catalog id and the IdP subjects are only known at run time, so a static seed can't wire the demo data. Solution: a small idempotent INTERNAL bootstrap surface (/internal/bootstrap/{users,teams,custom-roles,memberships}) mounted under the already-permitAll /internal/** path (in-network only, NOT the public secured management API), plus a run-team-matrix.sh that mints four in-network tokens, base64url-decodes each JWT 'sub', seeds a fixed demo catalog row into the catalog DB (the stable team-target), bootstraps the team+memberships through the internal API, then runs newman. Proves through the gateway: owner writes / viewer-member denied / custom-editor (team-scoped custom role) writes / non-member denied — roles resolved from real membership — plus the dogfood management path (owner manages, member 403). Keep the bootstrap clearly scoped as test scaffolding so the secured management API stays the demonstrated path.

The per-ticket workflow runs a clean-room/build check with 'git add -A' (or 'git add -A' to stage a diff for scanning) and ALSO records Mulch with 'ml record … && ml sync'. ml sync stages and commits whatever it considers part of the expertise update — but in practice it commits EVERYTHING currently staged, not just .mulch/. So a 'mulch: update expertise' commit silently swept in the ticket's source/docs/a git-mv folder rename three separate times this run, violating the hard rule that Mulch sync commits must touch .mulch/ ONLY (and mixing code into a commit titled 'mulch: …').
resolution: Before 'ml sync', ensure the index contains ONLY .mulch/ — run 'git restore --staged .' (unstage everything) then either let ml sync stage .mulch itself, or 'git add .mulch/' explicitly. If a mixed 'mulch: …' commit already happened, recover with: git reset --soft HEAD~1; git restore --staged .; git add .mulch/; git commit -m 'mulch: …'; then git add <the ticket's real paths> and commit the source separately. Order the per-ticket steps so the clean-room scan uses 'git add -A' + 'git diff --cached' + 'git restore --staged .' (leaving a CLEAN index) BEFORE doing the Mulch record/sync, so ml sync can't capture staged source.

title: Dynamic tag dictionary: three separable layers (definition / assignment / requirement), match-in-Rego, global+team-scoped
rationale: Phase-4.5 design, decided with the maintainer. Generalizes the source platform's tag machinery (study-only @AutoTag/TagDictionary/ResourceTag) but IMPROVES on it: the source only has compile-time system tag KEYS (no user-managed, team-scoped, runtime-defined tags). The clean design separates three concerns the source tangles in one package: (1) tag DEFINITION = a dictionary entry {key, scope, valueType(STRING|ENUM), cardinality(SINGLE|MULTI), allowedValues?}; scope is GLOBAL(system, seeded, immutable) vs TEAM(owner/admin-defined) — reusing the EXACT system-vs-team partial-unique-index pattern already shipped for role definitions (team_id IS NULL). (2) tag ASSIGNMENT = attaching validated values to a (sub-)resource on create/update, stored in the existing ResourceTags JSONB (which already supports scalar AND array => single/multi free). (3) tag REQUIREMENT = a role definition carries required-tags + a match mode ANY_OF/ALL_OF; a user carrying the role gains access when the resource's tags satisfy it. DECISIONS: match is evaluated IN REGO (some in = any-of/exists, every = all-of/forall) — the industry-standard semantics (AWS ForAnyValue:/ForAllValues:, Cerbos any/all/none, OpenFGA conditions) — making tags actually grant access and leading into Phase-7 ReBAC; dictionary is BOTH global+team-scoped; owner/admin DEFINE the dictionary (management capability) while members ASSIGN values (normal write), matching Databricks governed-tags/AWS tag-policy governance. This turn produces the design/decomposition package only (workflow-as-artifact); implementation runs separately.

name: Dictionary governance verb: team:define-tags (owner + admin), reusing the dogfooded capability ladder
description: Curating a team's tag dictionary is a MANAGEMENT capability, not a resource write. Add a 'team:define-tags' verb to the TeamRoleCapabilities ladder for BOTH owner and administrator (admins curate the vocabulary writers assign from — governed-tag model), distinct from owner-only 'team:define-roles' which shapes the access ladder itself. Because the verb shares the 'team:' prefix and team.rego is generic (verb in role_definition.permissions['team']), the policy needs NO logic change — only the ladder + doc + opa-test additions. The capability flows owner/admin -> EffectiveRoleService.managementRole -> TeamRoleDefinitionSupplier -> the dogfooded @OpaPreAuthorize. Keep the three layers separate: define = governance (this verb); assign = a normal resource write (no new capability); the grant = the role + the Rego match.

title: Fail-closed has two shapes: empty-for-deny (role/decision) vs reject (validation-input fetch)
rationale: A role/decision supplier (HttpRoleDefinitionSupplier) fails closed to Optional.empty(): the policy then default-denies — empty is the safe value. But a fetch whose result is a VALIDATION INPUT (the tag dictionary the catalog validates assigned tags against) must fail closed to a REJECTION, not an empty set: an empty applicable-set would make every tag illegal-by-absence or, worse, be misread as all-allowed — either way it WIDENS or corrupts legality. So TagDefinitionClient throws TagDefinitionFetchException on any non-200/timeout/refused/malformed; the catalog turns that into 503 and persists nothing. Rule of thumb: when the fetched value GATES a decision, empty=deny is fail-closed; when it CONSTRAINS what is legal, empty is unsafe — reject instead. Validation across the two example apps is by the wire CONTRACT (TagDefinitionView), not a shared class — a shared validator would force a non-additive library change.

name: Additive evolution of a public Jackson-serialized record (byte-for-byte back-compat)
description: To add fields to a published, OPA-input-serialized record (core.RoleDefinition) without breaking the wire or any caller: (1) add optional record components annotated @JsonProperty(snake_case) @JsonInclude(NON_EMPTY/NON_NULL) so when unused they are ABSENT and an old role serializes byte-for-byte as before; (2) normalize dependent fields to null when the feature is off — match_mode is null unless required_tags is non-empty, else defaults to ANY_OF — so the absent-field invariant holds and the stored row agrees with the resolved object; (3) keep the prior-arity constructor as a convenience delegate (new 3-arg -> 5-arg with empty/null) so every existing caller compiles unchanged; (4) Jackson fills missing record components with null on deserialize, which the compact constructor normalizes, so old payloads still parse. PROVE additivity with a whole-repo ./gradlew build (every old test unchanged) PLUS a byte-shape assertion (the serialized JSON has EXACTLY the old field names). This was the single allowed library change for the whole tag-dictionary slice; the other library modules stayed untouched (git diff --name-only).

name: ANY_OF / ALL_OF tag match in Rego (some-in / every) with vacuous back-compat + fail-closed
description: To match a role's required_tags ({key:[acceptable]}) against a resource whose tag value may be a SCALAR or an ARRAY, in OPA 1.x: (1) normalize the resource value to a SET — resource_tag_values(key) with three mutually-exclusive bodies (is_array -> {elements}, not is_array -> {scalar}, absent -> set()); (2) key_satisfied(key,acceptable) = existential intersection 'some v in resource_tag_values(key); v in acceptable'; (3) tags_satisfied for ANY_OF via 'some key,acceptable in required_tags; key_satisfied' (existential) and for ALL_OF via 'every key,acceptable in required_tags { key_satisfied }' (universal). Make the no-requirement case a SEPARATE vacuous body ('not has_required_tags' where has_required_tags := count(required_tags)>0) so untagged roles are unaffected (back-compat). Crucially: do NOT add an explicit error rule for a malformed requirement — let a present-but-unknown match_mode match none of the quantifier rules and not be vacuous, so tags_satisfied simply fails -> deny (fail-closed). 'allow' then requires BOTH the permission AND tags_satisfied. This is the OPA-native expression of attribute-based grants and the on-ramp to Phase-7 ReBAC-in-policy. Prove the decisive contrast with opa eval: same role, two resources differing only in tags -> one allow, one deny.

name: Per-instance tag-aware load-then-check (when the type-level @OpaPreAuthorize can't see the resource's tags)
description: The pre-invocation @OpaPreAuthorize is TYPE-LEVEL: it evaluates SpEL against method ARGUMENTS before the handler runs, so it cannot supply the resource's attributes (tags) to OPA. For a decision that depends on the resource's tags (a tag-based grant), do an explicit APP-LAYER load-then-check in the controller: load the entity, then call the library's OpaClient directly with the LOADED entity as the AbacContext.Resource (so its tags reach input.resource.attributes) and the role resolved via the governing PARENT (a Category is governed by its Catalog's team, so resolve on (catalog, catalogId), not the category id). This is EXAMPLE-APP code built on the library's public OpaClient + RoleDefinitionSupplier beans — NOT a library change; the general per-instance/hierarchical authorization path belongs in the library at Phase 5. Fail-closed: deny on no-subject / unresolved-role / OPA error. E2E shape that proves it: seed two tag-gated roles (ANY_OF + ALL_OF) and three differently-tagged resources at run time, then assert the decisive same-role/different-tags 200-vs-403 contrast through the gateway. Operational gotcha: tearing the compose rig down/up while the shared network is in use can drop the whole pool — bring base Postgres up first, then the rig, then re-run.

content: Structural decisions get an ADR as part of decomposition — written UP FRONT, not after. ADRs live in docs/architecture/adr/NNNN-short-title.md (lightly-MADR: Status / Context / Decision / Considered options WITH why-rejected / Consequences) with an index README. A decision is 'structural' (=> needs an ADR) when it would be expensive to reverse or surprising to a future reader: a schema/authority shape, a module/service boundary, where a check is evaluated (app vs Rego/policy), an additive-vs-breaking choice, or a deliberate 'we did NOT do X' with real alternatives weighed. Routine choices (naming, file layout, test lib) do NOT need one. WHY up front: a feature's 00-DESIGN/01-DECOMPOSITION are LIVING docs that get rewritten and git-mv'd to implemented/ on ship, so rationale buried there drifts; an ADR is IMMUTABLE — it pins the decision + rejected alternatives at a point in time and is SUPERSEDED (never edited) by a later ADR (flip the old status to 'Superseded by [[NNNN-...]]'). Heuristic: if you catch yourself writing a 'considered & rejected' list worth keeping, that's an ADR. The planning step is now: decomposition surfaces a fork -> write/update the ADR -> link it from 00-DESIGN. (Records 0001-0004 for the user-management entity graph / team-target / role-defs / tag dictionary were backfilled retroactively; going forward the ADR is authored with the decomposition.)

title: Phase 5 data-filtering planned: partial-eval (compile→DNF residual→JPA Specification) + batch, fail-closed, abstract OpaClient methods
rationale: Phase 5 (the advanced-library slice) is planned+decomposed in docs/to-do/planning/DATA-FILTERING/ (full package: index, 00-DESIGN, 01-DECOMPOSITION T1-T7, AUTONOMOUS-IMPLEMENTATION-PROMPT, 10-QA, 7 STATUS stubs) mirroring the four shipped slices 1:1. SCOPE (confirmed w/ maintainer): partial-eval + batch BOTH, NOT hierarchical ancestor-walk (that filters by ancestors; this slice filters by the row's OWN tags — the load-then-check CategoryAuthorizer stub stays). KEY DECISIONS: (1) Two ADDITIVE OpaClient methods — compile(AbacContext)->PartialResult via OPA Compile API (POST /v1/compile, query 'data/<type>/filter == true', unknowns=['input.resource'], resource OMITTED from input) and allowAll(List<AbacContext>)->List<Boolean> via a per-type 'bulk' rule. Make them ABSTRACT, not default methods, so a custom OpaClient cannot silently inherit a fail-OPEN filter. allow() + the @OpaPreAuthorize path stay byte-for-byte unchanged. (2) Neutral residual model in core (Spring-free): PartialResult{decision ALLOW_ALL|DENY_ALL|CONDITIONAL, List<Conjunction>} = DNF (OR-of-ANDs); Condition{path, Operator EQ|NEQ|IN|CONTAINS, value}. Mapping: compile result absent/{}->ALLOW_ALL; result.queries==[]->DENY_ALL; non-empty->CONDITIONAL. (3) ResidualSpecificationFactory in spring-data translates residual->Specification<T> over the tags JSONB (GIN-indexed since domain-model slice): EQ/IN via jsonb_extract_path_text(tags,'k'); CONTAINS (array tag) via the ? existence op jsonb_exists(tags->'k','v') — mirrors the TAG-DICTIONARY resource_tag_values scalar-vs-array normalize (mx-666644); intrinsic path (e.g. categoryId)->root.get(). ALLOW_ALL->no predicate; DENY_ALL->cb.disjunction() (always false). Postgres-only dialect (seam noted, second dialect not built). (4) FAIL-CLOSED is the load-bearing invariant: compile error->DENY_ALL (empty page); batch error->all-false; an UNSUPPORTED residual (operator outside the closed set / a non-input.resource ref) -> DENY_ALL, or with allowlistFallback=on -> exact batch re-check over a recognized-conjunct pre-filter. NEVER 'return everything' on error. The closed small operator set is deliberate (narrow-but-correct > wide-but-wrong: a mistranslated predicate = a silent data leak). (5) Three-layer separation: Compile-API+DNF in core, JSONB->Criteria in spring-data, the rego 'filter'/'bulk' entrypoints in policy. The differentiator (mx-15ee3e): the one comparable OSS project opa-data-filter is unmaintained. Lead-in still distinct from Phase-7 ReBAC-in-Rego (mx-723b5c). Planning branch: feature/void3110/plan-data-filtering.

title: Roadmap expanded: action enrichment = Phase 6 (affordance map via response advice + action registry + x-implements DTO marker); two ADRs pinned (0005 partial-eval, 0006 three-layer)
rationale: Roadmap grown along two routes (maintainer ask): tech topics + user stories, anchored by ADRs. KEY ADDITIONS: (1) ACTION ENRICHMENT as a new Phase 6 (bumps publish 6->7, ReBAC 7->8), planning note docs/to-do/planning/ACTION-ENRICHMENT (direction set, not yet decomposed; sequenced after Phase 5 because it is the FIRST consumer of the Phase-5 batch primitive OpaClient.allowAll). Enrichment = attach a {action:allowed} affordance map to a returned resource/page so a UI renders the right buttons. It is AFFORDANCE, NOT enforcement (enforcement = ADR 0006 three layers). Decided shape: a response decorator/ResponseBodyAdvice (automatic, not per-endpoint boilerplate); action source = a per-resource-type ACTION REGISTRY (generalizes the source platform's ActionName enum + ResourceTypeActions; doubles as a validation allowlist; superior to role-permissions-only because it can report delete:false for an ungranted verb). (2) THE KEY MECHANISM for fitting enrichment to OpenAPI codegen: stamp resource DTOs with an x-implements vendor extension so the org.openapi.generator 'spring' generator makes the generated POJO implement a library marker interface (e.g. Enrichable) — confirmed against the source platform's external-credentials DTO which stamps java.lang.AutoCloseable via 'x-implements: [java.lang.AutoCloseable]' + 'x-closeable: true'. The advice detects Enrichable returns, batch-evals, injects _actions. App opts in with ONE x-implements line in its spec — no DTO hand-editing/post-processing. Open Q held for Phase-6 planning: the envelope shape (inline _actions vs a wrapping Authorized<T>). (3) USER STORIES route: docs/to-do/planning/USER-STORIES.md — the PRODUCT lens over the tech roadmap; personas (viewer/editor/owner-admin/super-admin/integrator) + epics A-F each tagged to its delivering phase (A=P3 enforcement, B=P4 team roles, C=P4.5 tags, D=P5 list filtering, E=P6 enrichment, F=P7 publish). (4) ADRs authored UP FRONT per our own convention (mx — the ADR-in-decomposition convention): 0005 partial-eval->JPA Specification (pins the DATA-FILTERING fork: compile API->DNF residual->Specification over tags JSONB, fail-closed, abstract-not-default OpaClient methods), 0006 the three-layer enforcement model (gateway coarse -> app @OpaPreAuthorize/load-then-check -> DB partial-eval; THE PRINCIPLE: the app NEVER trusts the gateway, re-decides every single-resource return against the loaded resource to stop horizontal privilege escalation on a guessed ID — the gateway is defense-in-depth, not the decision). 0005/0006 are the first ADRs written up-front (0001-0004 were retroactive). Action-enrichment ADR PENDING (written with its decomposition). Branch: feature/void3110/plan-data-filtering (continuation).

title: Coarse-grained permission categories (READ/WRITE/TAG/GRANT) + five-tier role-level ceiling model + deny-overrides; subset rule scoped to the senior tier only
rationale: Designed via grill-me + web research (AWS/Azure/GCP/GitHub/Heroku/K8s). For the catalog domain (Catalog->Category->Product), the permission model: (1) FOUR coarse CATEGORIES that expand to fine actions — READ {view,list}, WRITE {create,update,delete}, TAG {define-tags,assign-tags}, GRANT {assign-roles}. Named GRANT (not MANAGE — MANAGE is ambiguous between manage-config and manage-access; every platform fences 'grant access to others' as a separate top capability: AWS Permissions-management, Azure Owner-vs-Contributor NotActions Microsoft.Authorization/*, GCP setIamPolicy, GitHub Admin, K8s admin-creates-RoleBindings). TAG (not CURATE) for plainness + matches AWS 'Tagging' access level + the shipped team:define-tags (ADR 0004). (2) GRANT MODEL = categories-only (NO a-la-carte individual-action grants) + DENY-OVERRIDES on top (Azure Actions/NotActions): effective_actions(type) = expand(granted_categories) \ denied_actions; allow if requested in effective. Denial is a global hard veto applied last. Rationale: survives new actions gracefully (a new action added to WRITE is auto-included unless denied — Azure's documented reason), lossless UI round-trip (store intent=categories not effect=actions), one grant shape. (3) EXPANSION lives in OPA: store category tokens; expansion table in OPA data (editable, no redeploy); Rego does expand-minus-deny — the teachable 'OPA expands coarse->fine' demo. (4) role_level = a PERMISSION CEILING/TEMPLATE, not free integer: owner picks level -> the ceiling categories auto-check and LOCK in the UI (higher disabled/uncheckable) -> owner refines DOWNWARD only via deny-overrides. FIVE authored tiers + owner reserved: reader(10) ceiling {READ}; member(20) {READ,WRITE,TAG}; senior(25) {READ,WRITE,TAG} + a constrained assign-members power; administrator(30) {READ,WRITE,TAG,GRANT}; owner=reserved root (authors role DEFINITIONS, assigns anything, transfer-ownership). (5) TWO FENCES (invariants): define-roles (authoring) = OWNER-ONLY, never a category, never delegatable (decided against delegating to admins — complicates trust analysis hugely); GRANT (assign roles) tops out at ADMINISTRATOR — senior canNOT hold/assign GRANT, so senior can only onboard member-or-lower roles and self-replication of assignment power is structurally impossible. (6) TWO ASSIGNMENT GATES, each one job: role_level strict '<' = cross-tier seniority (admin can't add admin); SUBSET RULE on effective (expanded-minus-denied) permission sets = used ONLY at the senior tier to order which member-roles a senior may hand out. KEY: subset is OPTIONAL complexity that exists to buy EXACTLY ONE feature (the senior delegate persona) — drop senior and you can drop subset and run on role_level alone. Personas (dev team): PM=owner, lead/architect=admin, senior-dev=senior, mid-dev/analyst=member, stakeholder=reader. ADDITIVITY: reuses the shipped role_level attribute (owner40/admin30/member20/viewer10 seeds) and the {type:[verbs]} permissions shape (a category token is new, a plain action token still works). The effective_actions expansion is reused at BOTH decision time and assignment-subset time (one function). Leads to ADR 0007 (planned, Phase ~6/7) + user stories in USER-STORIES.

description: Pre-implementation audit of shipped code before Phase-5 (data filtering) surfaced two reconciliation gotchas the plan didn't anticipate: (a) ./gradlew build goes RED the moment OpaClient gains abstract methods, because two test beans implement it as lambdas; (b) a naively-derived partial-eval 'filter' rule would inherit the shipped 'allow' rule's subject-roles fallback and return the WHOLE TABLE for a request with no role definition — a fail-OPEN list leak.
resolution: Both baked into the DATA-FILTERING plan. (1) BUILD-BREAKER: OpaClient is currently a single-method functional interface; two test beans implement it as LAMBDAS (PermissiveSecurityTestConfig.allowAllOpaClient in catalog, AbacTestConfig.inProcessTeamOpaClient in user-service) plus a named StubOpaClient in the starter test. Adding ADR-0005 abstract compile()+allowAll() makes OpaClient NON-functional, so both lambdas fail to compile; convert all three test impls to named/anonymous classes (compile->denyAll, allowAll->all-false as stubs) in the same commit as the interface change. 'Additive to the library contract' != 'zero-touch for tests'. (2) FAIL-OPEN LIST LEAK: shipped category/catalog/product.rego 'allow' has a subject-roles fallback (not has_role_definition -> grant read from JWT roles). The Phase-5 'filter' rule must be ROLE-DEFINITION-ONLY (model on team.rego, which dropped the fallback) so a missing role def -> DENY_ALL -> empty list. (3) Residual Specification must be AND-ed with the existing path scoping (findByCatalogId/findByCategoryId), never replace it; resolve role on the governing parent like CategoryAuthorizer. (4) Sequencing: Phase 5 ships BEFORE Phase 6.5, so 'filter' stays FLAT-VERB (category:read) — category expansion (ADR 0007) is a later additive retrofit; don't anticipate it. (5) allowAll is a SHARED primitive (Phase-6 enrichment consumes it) — design it general-public. All baked into DATA-FILTERING/{00-DESIGN,01-DECOMPOSITION,AUTONOMOUS-IMPLEMENTATION-PROMPT,10-QA-TEST-CASES} + cross-referenced to ADRs 0005/0006/0007.

name: OPA Compile-API partial-eval → neutral DNF residual (fail-closed at the empty-result boundary)
description: Translate OPA's Compile API (POST /v1/compile, query 'data.<type>.filter == true', unknowns=['input.resource'], resource OMITTED from input) into a Spring-free PartialResult{decision ALLOW_ALL|DENY_ALL|CONDITIONAL, List<Conjunction>} = DNF (OR-of-ANDs), Condition{path, Operator EQ|NEQ|IN|CONTAINS, value}. THE VERIFIED RESULT-SHAPE MAPPING (probed against OPA 1.10.1, and it is the OPPOSITE of what an intuitive reading suggests — getting it wrong is a fail-OPEN whole-table leak): {"result":{}} (empty, no queries key) = query UNSATISFIABLE = DENY_ALL (NOT allow-all!); {"result":{"queries":[[]]}} (a query whose conjunction is EMPTY) = unconditionally true = ALLOW_ALL; {"result":{"queries":[[expr,...]]}} = residual = CONDITIONAL. So ALLOW_ALL must emerge from EXACTLY ONE place — an explicit empty/tautological conjunction — and every other branch (absent result / no queries / unsupported term / any transport-parse error) returns denyAll(). AST per expression: {terms:[opRef, operandA, operandB]}; operator var = eq/equal (EQ), neq (NEQ), internal.member_2 (IN, from 'x in {set}'); 'negated':true folds eq->neq; one operand is a ref into input.resource.* ([{var input},{string resource},{string attributes/<intrinsic>},...]) the other a literal (string/number/boolean/set). Map attributes.<k> -> tags.<k>; an intrinsic (id) stays a column path. CRITICAL: because input.resource is the unknown, the residual ALWAYS includes eq('<type>', input.resource.type) — drop it as a tautology (we scope the SQL to one type), treat any other constraint on type as unsupported->deny. Closed operator set: any unrecognized operator/ref/literal poisons the WHOLE residual -> denyAll() (narrow-but-correct > wide-but-wrong; a mistranslated predicate is a silent data leak). Make compile()+allowAll() ABSTRACT (not default) on OpaClient so a custom client can't inherit a fail-open filter. GOTCHA: a record's static factory method must NOT share a name with one of its boolean component accessors (ExprResult.unsupported() factory clashes with the unsupported() accessor) -> rename to notSupported().

name: Residual DNF → JPA Specification over the tags JSONB column (Postgres), SQL/Rego agreement on scalar-vs-array
description: Translate a neutral PartialResult{ALLOW_ALL|DENY_ALL|CONDITIONAL, DNF clauses} into a Spring Data JpaSpecificationExecutor Specification over the tags JSONB column, with NO OPA-wire knowledge in spring-data (clean module boundary: core=Compile API+DNF, spring-data=JSONB→Criteria). Mapping: ALLOW_ALL->Specification.where(null) (no predicate; the caller's path scope still applies AND-ed); DENY_ALL or a null residual->(r,q,cb)->cb.disjunction() (always-false=match-none, the fail-closed shape); CONDITIONAL->cb.or(cb.and(conds)...) over the DNF, with an EMPTY conjunction short-circuiting to cb.conjunction() (always-true). Per-condition via JPA Criteria function() with BOUND literals (no SQL strings, injection-safe, dialect-portable): tags.<k> EQ/NEQ -> cb.equal/notEqual(cb.function('jsonb_extract_path_text',String,root.get('tags'),cb.literal(k)), v); IN -> extractText(...).in(values); CONTAINS (array membership) -> cb.isTrue(cb.function('jsonb_exists',Boolean, cb.function('jsonb_extract_path',Object,tags,literal(k)), literal(v))) i.e. the ? existence operator; an intrinsic (non-tags) path -> root.get('<field>') compare. Centralize the JSONB fn names in a package-private JsonPathDialect seam (Postgres impl) so a 2nd dialect is a seam not a rewrite (don't build a 2nd dialect). CRITICAL SEMANTIC: the Postgres ? operator on a JSONB STRING scalar tests STRING EQUALITY (on an ARRAY it tests element membership) — so 'region CONTAINS emea' matches BOTH a scalar region=='emea' row AND a [emea,amer] array row. This is CORRECT and required: it AGREES with the single-decision Rego whose resource_tag_values normalizes a scalar to a singleton set (mx-666644), so the LIST and a single-GET decide the SAME rows (ADR-0005/0006). Assert it in the IT, don't 'fix' it. TEST POSTURE: a Mockito Criteria-capture unit test (stub cb.function/equal/and/or, verify the calls) PLUS a mandatory Testcontainers IT against REAL Postgres+JSONB (never H2 — jsonb_* and ? are Postgres-only) seeding scalar+array+multi-key rows and asserting EXACT surviving row sets for EQ/IN/CONTAINS/DNF/ALLOW_ALL/DENY_ALL. For the IT in this non-app library module: a nested @SpringBootApplication + @DataJpaTest(replace=NONE) + @Testcontainers, AND @EnableJpaAuditing(dateTimeProviderRef) with a DateTimeProvider returning OffsetDateTime (createdAt is @CreatedDate nullable=false; LocalDateTime provider throws, mx-5fb01d), AND the module's test task needs TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=true + the resolved podman DOCKER_HOST (copy the example modules' resolveDockerHost()).

name: AbacQueryService seam: compile→Specification→query, AND-with-scope, fail-closed allowlist via a fullySupported flag
description: The list-authorization seam tying OPA partial-eval to the DB (layer 3 of the three-layer model). findAuthorized(JpaSpecificationExecutor<T extends AbacDataObject> repo, Specification<T> scope, AbacContext queryContext): (1) opaClient.compile(ctx)->residual; (2) ResidualSpecificationFactory.from(residual)->authzSpec; (3) repo.findAll(scope.and(authzSpec)). TWO LOAD-BEARING INVARIANTS: (a) AND-NEVER-REPLACE — always scope.and(authzSpec), never a bare findAll(authzSpec), so the caller's path scoping (catalogId/categoryId) is preserved and no cross-scope row leaks (prove with an IT: authz=emea AND scope=apac -> empty). (b) NEVER FAIL-OPEN — a partialEval.enabled=false kill-switch degrades to the COARSE pre-Phase-5 path (one opaClient.allow(ctx) check then scope-only), deny->List.of() BEFORE any findAll; the allowlist finisher engages ONLY on !residual.fullySupported() && allowlistFallback. THE fullySupported FLAG (additive core change to PartialResult): a 3rd record component boolean fullySupported (default true via a preserved 2-arg convenience ctor so T1/T3 stay byte-compatible) + a PartialResult.unsupported() factory = a fail-closed DENY_ALL FLAGGED not-fully-SQL. CompileResponseParser returns unsupported() (not plain denyAll()) when it hits an untranslatable term; a clean empty result stays a fully-supported denyAll(). This is how the allowlist escape hatch stays fail-closed: residual not-fully-SQL + allowlist ON -> fetch scoped candidates, build per-row AbacContext (resource=the loaded AbacDataObject's type/id/attributes, same subject/action/roleDef), opaClient.allowAll(perRow), drop false rows (a short/mismatched batch from the client's all-false-on-error also drops rows). allowlist OFF -> just deny (empty). NEVER a blind fetch-all, never a wider set. Bound findAuthorized <T extends AbacDataObject> (the plan said bare <T>) so per-row contexts can be built. Settings carrier: a PartialEvalSettings(enabled, allowlistFallback) record with defaults()=both-on, which the starter binds its partialEval.* properties onto. Test: mock repo + a 3-method stub OpaClient (compile/allow/allowAll programmable) for U20-U24; a Testcontainers IT proving two subjects -> different disjoint row sets + the AND-with-scope no-leak.

name: Partial-eval-friendly 'filter' rego rule: role-def-only (fail-closed), flat-verb, scalar+array consistency via member_2 operand side
description: The Phase-5 list-filtering entrypoint added ALONGSIDE the single-decision 'allow' (additive, allow untouched). Two deliberate differences from 'allow': (1) ROLE-DEFINITION-ONLY — 'filter' starts with has_role_definition and has NO subject-roles fallback (model on team.rego). A list request with no role definition partial-evaluates to {} -> DENY_ALL -> EMPTY list, never the whole table (the fail-OPEN leak guard from mx-ff73f1). Prove with opa test: filter false for no-role-def, AND a contrast test that 'allow' DOES grant the same read via its fallback. (2) PARTIAL-EVAL-FRIENDLY tag match: do NOT reuse the single-decision tags_satisfied (its resource_tag_values scalar-vs-array normalize compiles to is_array + set-comprehension AST that a closed-operator residual parser can't translate -> unsupported/deny). Instead write a filter-specific two-body helper filter_key_satisfied(key,acceptable): body A 'input.resource.attributes[key] == v' (scalar), body B 'v in input.resource.attributes[key]' (array). This compiles to a clean 2-disjunct DNF residual: eq(v, attr) + internal.member_2(v, attr). KEY PARSER RULE: internal.member_2 operand SIDE decides the operator — member_2(resourceRef, {literals}) = 'row's value is one of these' = IN (jsonb_extract_path_text ... IN); member_2(literal, resourceRef) = 'this literal is in the row's value(s)' = CONTAINS (jsonb_exists, the ? op). The ? operator matches a JSONB string scalar (string-equality) AND an array element, so CONTAINS covers both — and the two-body filter means concrete rego eval also matches both. NET: list filtering and a single-GET decide the SAME rows for scalar and array tags (ADR-0005/0006 consistency). A negated membership -> unsupported. Also add a 'bulk := [allow with input as item | some item in input.items]' rule for the batch/allowlist primitive (positional decisions; opa test [true,false] + empty->[]). FLAT-VERB only (category:read) — category expansion (READ/WRITE/TAG/GRANT) is a later additive retrofit (ADR 0007 / Phase 6.5), don't anticipate. App adoption: a CategoryListAuthorizer (example code on the public AbacQueryService) resolves the role on the GOVERNING PARENT (catalog, catalogId) like CategoryAuthorizer, builds a query ctx (resource UNKNOWN), and AND-s a catalogId(+parentId) scope Specification into findAuthorized. GOTCHA: in OPA 1.x 'in' is reserved — don't name a test var 'in'.

name: e2e list-filtering matrix: two subjects, same endpoint, different row sets through the gateway
description: The Phase-5 data-filtering e2e (run-filter-matrix.sh + data-filter-matrix.postman_collection.json), modeled on run-tag-matrix.sh but asserting LIST row SETS not single 200/403. Needs the full rig ENABLE_OIDC=1 ENABLE_USER_SERVICE=1 ./deploy.sh up --pods 2. At run time: mint in-network tokens (issuer keycloak:8888 caveat) for owner(editor)/reader-emea(viewer)/reader-apac(demo)/stranger(OUTSIDER — the rig's standing unbound user, also run-team-matrix.sh's non-member); seed a fixed demo catalog row (the team-target) via psql into opa-abac-postgres; via the user-service /internal/bootstrap/* create a team + two single-region-gated custom roles (emea-reader requiredTags region ANY_OF [emea]; apac-reader [apac]) + bind owner->owner, the two readers->their gated roles, and DELIBERATELY leave the stranger UNBOUND (no membership -> no role definition); create three region-tagged Categories (emea/apac/amer) through the gateway with the owner token; run newman. The 4 list assertions on GET /catalogs/{id}/categories: reader-emea sees ONLY the emea row (1), reader-apac ONLY apac (1, a DIFFERENT set — the decisive proof the residual is in SQL not a post-filter), owner ALL three, stranger [] (the fail-closed boundary: filter rule has no subject-roles fallback). GOTCHAS: (1) deploy.sh only rebuilds the app image if it's ABSENT (image_exists || build_image) — after changing app code you MUST run ./deploy.sh build to force a rebuild, else the pods run stale code; (2) ./profile.sh up (base Postgres) must run BEFORE ./deploy.sh up; (3) restart/redeploy OPA after editing category.rego (the rig mounts it but --watch doesn't always reload — confirm via POST /v1/compile that the filter rule is present); (4) keep the runtime-captured category ids in the collection variable scope, NOT the env file (env scope shadows collection -> empty-id URLs). DOC NAMING: the GUIDE note must NOT share a basename with the planning-index note — both were DATA-FILTERING.md (collision); rename the guide to a distinct basename (PARTIAL-EVALUATION-FILTERING) like the TAG-DICTIONARY plan vs TAG-BASED-AUTHORIZATION guide precedent.

Live e2e filter-matrix run surfaced two issues the unit/IT tests (synthetic role-defs) could not: (1) the demo's allow-all category lister bound to the SYSTEM owner role got an EMPTY list; (2) reruns drifted the row counts.
resolution: (1) The system 'owner' role resolves to {permissions:{catalog:[read,write]}} — it has NO 'category' key. The Phase-5 'filter' rule checks '"read" in permissions[input.resource.type]' with resource.type='category', so under the system owner the residual is DENY_ALL -> empty list. This is CORRECT (catalog-verbs != category-verbs in the role model), not a filter bug. Fix the DEMO: give the allow-all subject a custom 'curator' role with ungated category:[read,write] (no requiredTags -> ALLOW_ALL residual on categories). Lesson: an 'allow-all over type X' subject needs a role that actually grants verbs on type X; a parent-type grant doesn't cascade to child-type list filtering. (2) The create-category endpoint isn't idempotent, so the matrix must DELETE the demo catalog's categories before seeding (DELETE FROM category WHERE catalog_id=...) — otherwise reruns accumulate rows and 'exactly N' assertions drift. With the clean seed the matrix is stable across reruns (16/16, verified 3x). BONUS newman gotcha: inject runtime ids via --env-var (environment scope) but read them in test scripts with pm.variables.get() (resolves across scopes) NOT pm.collectionVariables.get() (collection scope only — sees the empty declared default); and don't declare the ids as collection variables at all (their empty default shadows nothing but is noise).

name: AncestorResolver SPI: fail-closed walk owned by the library, data-access via a tiny source SPI, two interchangeable impls
description: N-level hierarchical authorization resolves a leaf's root-first, leaf-excluded ancestor chain (input.resource.ancestors) behind an AncestorResolver SPI. The library owns the correctness-critical WALK (ordering, leaf-exclusion, mandatory cycle detection, mandatory depth bound) and is fail-closed by THROWING AncestorResolutionException — never returning a partial/truncated chain (a truncation could under- or over-grant; callers treat throw as 'no inheritance ⇒ direct grant only', never 'allow'). Per-app DATA ACCESS is a separate one-method source SPI so the resolver stays table-agnostic and unit-testable with in-memory stubs: LtreePathSource(pathOf type,id→Optional<String>) for the default LtreeAncestorResolver (decode a denormalized ltree path in ONE indexed read; throw on missing/NULL/malformed/leaf-mismatch/over-depth) and ParentLinkSource(parentOf type,id→Optional<ParentRef>) for RecursiveCteAncestorResolver (walk live parent_id adjacency hop-by-hop, visited-set cycle detection incl self-loop, depth counter; correct-by-construction on re-parent, no denormalized state). ltree labels allow only [A-Za-z0-9_], so a UUID id is encoded as 32 dash-free hex digits (HierarchyLabels, shared encode/decode so the T3 path-maintainer and the decoder can't drift). Package opa-abac-spring-data.hierarchy imports only core.ParentRef + java.util — zero OPA-wire/residual/Specification coupling; the Phase-5 list filter is untouched (that's Slice 5.5-B). Tested with pure-JUnit (both impls, every fail-closed path) + Testcontainers real Postgres + the ltree extension (never H2).

name: Opt-in AbstractHierarchicalEntity + atomic ltree subtree re-parent (path maintenance off the entity)
description: Hierarchy is an OPT-IN persistent base AbstractHierarchicalEntity extends AbstractSecuredEntity, adding a denormalized ltree 'path' column (map String with @Column(columnDefinition=ltree) + @ColumnTransformer(write="?::ltree") so a bound String lands in the ltree column without an implicit cast) + abstract abacParent() + selfLabel(). Non-hierarchical secured entities keep extending AbstractSecuredEntity and pay nothing (no path column). A leaf's missing parent FK (e.g. Product has no catalogId) is solved by the path encoding the full lineage, not a redundant column. Path MAINTENANCE lives OFF the entity in a HierarchicalPathMaintainer service (a @MappedSuperclass can't run native SQL; keeping it in a service mirrors AbstractCrudService.mutate write-centralization and makes re-parent one transactional unit): assignPath derives path=parent.path||self-label, throwing on a declared-but-missing parent path (broken lineage, fail-closed); reparent rewrites the ENTIRE moved subtree ATOMICALLY in ONE ltree UPDATE 'SET path = CASE WHEN nlevel(path)=oldDepth THEN newSelfPath ELSE newSelfPath || subpath(path, oldDepth) END WHERE path <@ oldSelfPath' — the CASE is REQUIRED because subpath(path, nlevel(path)) is an invalid ltree position for the moved node's own row. A re-parent under one's own descendant is rejected up-front (cycle guard). Atomicity is a single-statement DB guarantee: a UNIQUE(path) collision mid-rewrite rolls the whole UPDATE back (tree unchanged) — proven by a Testcontainers IT using TransactionTemplate for COMMITTED units of work (not @DataJpaTest rollback) so the re-parent and its rollback are observable across transactions. Only the table identifier is interpolated (regex-validated); all values are bound params.

An ltree subtree re-parent UPDATE 'SET path = newPrefix || subpath(path, oldDepth) WHERE path <@ oldSelfPath' fails with Postgres 'ERROR: invalid positions' on the MOVED NODE's own row, because subpath(path, offset) requires offset < nlevel(path) and for the moved node nlevel(path)==oldDepth (offset==length).
resolution: Guard the moved node's own row with a CASE: 'SET path = CASE WHEN nlevel(path)=oldDepth THEN CAST(newSelfPath AS ltree) ELSE CAST(newSelfPath AS ltree) || subpath(path, oldDepth) END'. The node itself gets just newSelfPath (empty descendant suffix); descendants (nlevel>oldDepth) get the valid subpath. Caught by the Testcontainers re-parent IT.

name: Opt-in default-off starter wiring for hierarchy: @ConditionalOnBean(source) resolver selection by property
description: Wire N-level hierarchy in the OPA-ABAC starter as a TWO-PART opt-in, default-off. (1) A HierarchyAutoConfiguration nested in OpaAbacAutoConfiguration is gated on @ConditionalOnProperty(opa.abac.hierarchy.enabled=true) WITHOUT matchIfMissing (so absent config ⇒ no beans) AND @ConditionalOnClass(JpaSpecificationExecutor). (2) The AncestorResolver is @ConditionalOnBean on the app-provided data-access SOURCE (LtreePathSource for resolver=ltree default, ParentLinkSource for resolver=cte) — the library can't know the app's table mapping, so it only wires a resolver once the app supplies the matching source; the HierarchicalAuthorizer is @ConditionalOnBean(AncestorResolver). All beans @ConditionalOnMissingBean so an app-supplied resolver/authorizer overrides everything. Properties live in OpaAbacProperties.Hierarchy (enabled/resolver/maxDepth + an inheritable map childType->[ancestorType]); inheritable is surfaced as config but consumed by the REGO (OPA data), not the Java wiring (the starter only uses enabled/resolver/maxDepth to build beans). Regenerate spring-configuration-metadata.json via the configuration-processor. The Phase-5 partial-eval beans/properties stay untouched (hierarchy is purely additive). Verified by ApplicationContextRunner: default-off, ltree/cte selection, no-source→no-resolver, user-override-wins, property binding.

name: Rego N-level inheritance clause + deny-overrides: granted-then-narrow, opt-in via data, ancestors-in-input
description: To add ancestor inheritance + deny-overrides to a per-type OPA policy WITHOUT breaking the existing direct/fallback/tag logic: restructure to a single 'allow if { granted; not denied }' where 'granted' is an OR of rule bodies (direct_grant, inherited_grant [+ tags_satisfied for tag-gated types], subject-roles fallback). The inherited_grant reads input.resource.ancestors (root-first, leaf-excluded {type,id} list; the role is resolved ONCE on the governing root so role_definition.permissions is keyed by ANCESTOR type) and is gated OPT-IN by data.<pkg>.inheritable[leaftype][ancestortype] — absent ⇒ no inheritance, so with no inheritable data the policy behaves EXACTLY as the pre-hierarchy direct-only decision. deny-overrides is the final narrowing AND: 'denied if input.resource.attributes.abac_deny == true'. Keep OPA 1.x style (no imports), default deny, and any filter/bulk partial-eval entrypoints UNCHANGED (deny-overrides + inheritance are single-decision concerns). GOTCHA for opa test: bundling the inheritable data as JSON under /policies makes inheritance always-on, so the 'opt-in OFF ⇒ deny' tests must explicitly override 'with data.<pkg>.inheritable as {}'. inheritable ships as data JSON files under the OPA policies dir (loaded with the policies); mirror it in the app config for one source of truth.

name: Cross-table ltree subtree re-parent + GiST index + recursive-CTE backfill (multi-table hierarchy adoption)
description: When a resource hierarchy spans MULTIPLE tables (Catalog/Category in one shape, Products in another), an atomic ltree subtree re-parent must rewrite the moved subtree in the PRIMARY table AND its descendant rows in the OTHER table(s) — a single-table UPDATE ... WHERE path <@ oldSelfPath leaves cross-table descendants pointing at the stale lineage. Library method HierarchicalPathMaintainer.reparentDescendantsInTable(table, oldSelfPath, newParent) does the descendant-only rewrite (no new-parent/cycle validation, no min-row requirement — that's the primary reparent() call's job); call both in the same transaction. App-side re-parent ordering that avoids the managed entity overwriting the native rewrite: (1) set parentId on the managed entity + saveAndFlush, (2) entityManager.clear(), (3) native subtree path rewrite, (4) re-read fresh. Liquibase ltree adoption gotchas: ltree's <@ containment operator needs a GiST index (NOT GIN — GIN is for the JSONB tags); backfill nested paths with a recursive CTE; CREATE EXTENSION ltree before the path columns; map the path as a String with @Column(columnDefinition=ltree)+@ColumnTransformer(write='?::ltree'); ddl-auto: validate boots clean as the entity↔migration proof. Read the path via getResultList() not getResultStream() (a lazy stream raises 'ResultSet is closed' after the context is cleared).
