description: The Phase-5.5-A deny-overrides control tag (input.resource.attributes.abac_deny == true) cannot be assigned through the catalog gateway's create/update path: the Phase-4.5 TagAssignmentService validates every tag key against the dynamic tag dictionary and rejects an unknown key with 422 'Unknown tag key abac_deny (no applicable definition)'. So the hierarchy e2e's deny-overrides scenario fails at category creation when it tries to POST tags:{abac_deny:true}.
resolution: abac_deny is an OPERATIONAL control flag (a policy deny-override), not a user-facing business tag, so it should not go through dictionary validation. In the e2e, create the Category plainly then set the flag OUT-OF-BAND via SQL: UPDATE category SET tags = jsonb_set(coalesce(tags,'{}'::jsonb),'{abac_deny}','true') WHERE id=... (the same way the matrix seeds catalogs). For a real deployment, either register abac_deny as a reserved/system tag key in the dictionary, or carry the deny flag on a dedicated column instead of the JSONB tags. Also: make e2e create helpers surface the raw response on a non-id body (don't pipe straight into a python ['id'] that throws a bare KeyError traceback).

description: A multi-table ltree re-parent service (CatalogHierarchyService.reparentCategory) read the moving Category with the UNLOCKED categories.findById then mutated + @Version-bumped that same row (setParentId + saveAndFlush) before the native subtree path rewrite. This deviates from the repo's documented lock-first mutate posture (AbstractCrudService.mutate / getByIdForUpdate: 'lock the row FOR UPDATE so two concurrent mutations serialize and neither sees a stale @Version'). CategoryRepository already extends LockableJpaRepository so findByIdForUpdate was available and unused; the row write was only optimistically guarded (the native ltree UPDATE locks by path AFTER the entity mutate, not a JPA pessimistic read that refreshes the in-session @Version). Guides billed the re-parent as 'atomic', overselling an optimistic-only row guard.
resolution: Make the FIRST entity-touching read in a re-parent/mutate flow a pessimistic-locked read: categories.findByIdForUpdate(categoryId) instead of findById, so concurrent operations on the same row serialize at the SELECT ... FOR UPDATE lock. Rule of thumb: any @Transactional method whose first act is read-then-write of a row that other writers can touch should lead with the locked read (the documented mutate posture), not rely on optimistic @Version alone — especially when downstream native SQL (here the ltree subtree rewrite) makes a half-applied state visible to a racing reader.

description: An e2e gateway assertion can PASS without exercising the feature under test (CUT). The hierarchy matrix's 'inheritance -> 200' check seeded the reader role with BOTH catalog:[read] AND category:[read]; since category.rego decides allow via 'granted if direct_grant' where direct_grant = verb in permissions[resource.type], the direct category:read fired and the 200 proved a DIRECT grant — the test would still pass if the new inherited_grant clause + the inheritable data file were deleted. The rego UNIT test correctly isolated inheritance (a catalog-ONLY role) but the e2e did not. This is the 'asserts shape (200) not the cut (inheritance-vs-direct)' agentic-laziness failure mode the autonomous-run lens watches for.
resolution: Seed the e2e so the asserted outcome can ONLY come from the CUT: give the reader catalog:[read] ONLY (no direct category grant), so a readable Category proves inherited_grant. Verify by reading back the seeded role from the user-mgmt DB (here: {"catalog":["read"]}). General rule for allow/deny matrices: the role/tag seed must make the decisive request's success attributable to the new clause alone — mirror how the rego unit test isolates it, don't grant a superset that lets the old direct path satisfy the assertion.

title: NEXT TOPIC: Slice 5.5-B — hierarchy-aware LIST filter (subtreeSpec composed with the Phase-5 residual). 5.5-A is shipped+merged.
rationale: Slice 5.5-A (single-resource N-level hierarchical authorization) is SHIPPED and merged to main (PR #14 squash 0eca324; package at docs/to-do/implemented/HIERARCHY-SINGLE-RESOURCE/; guide docs/guides/HIERARCHICAL-AUTHORIZATION.md). Repo at handoff: on main, clean tree, all green (./gradlew build, opa test 72/72, CI build(21), all 5 newman gateway matrices). The maintainer's NEXT topic is Slice 5.5-B: make the Phase-5 partial-eval LIST filter hierarchy-aware so a grant on an ancestor WIDENS which rows a list endpoint (e.g. GET .../products or .../categories) returns — not just single-resource checks. DESIGN IS ALREADY PINNED by ADR 0008 (docs/architecture/adr/0008-hierarchical-resource-authorization.md, 'How it composes with the Phase-5 list filter'): the OPA residual STAYS TAG-ONLY (CompileResponseParser / ResidualSpecificationFactory / the closed operator set are UNCHANGED — 'is this row in an allowed subtree' is a fact about LINEAGE, not tags), and hierarchy widening is a SEPARATE, APP-BUILT subtreeSpec OR-ed into the query: combined = scope.and( tagResidual.or(subtreeSpec) ).and( notDenied ). subtreeSpec = ltree 'path <@ <allowed-subtree-roots>' (the LtreeAncestorResolver/path already shipped in 5.5-A) OR 'id IN (<descendant-id-set>)' (CTE), where the allowed-subtree-roots are resolved ONCE per list call from the subject's inheritable ancestor grants. FAIL-CLOSED by construction: if hierarchy resolution fails, subtreeSpec is an empty (false) predicate and the result falls back to the NARROWER tag-only filter — never wider. WHAT 5.5-B BUILDS ON (all shipped in 5.5-A): the ltree path column + GiST index + the AncestorResolver SPI + AbstractHierarchicalEntity + the inheritable config + opt-in default-off. The single-resource HierarchicalAuthorizer stays as-is. WHERE THE SEAM LIVES: AbacQueryService is the Phase-5 list seam (findAuthorized: compile->residual->Specification->findAll, scope.and(authzSpec)); 5.5-B adds the subtreeSpec OR-branch there or in an app-level CategoryListAuthorizer-style composer (CategoryListAuthorizer currently does tag-only list filtering and was deliberately UNTOUCHED in 5.5-A). OPEN QUESTIONS for the design session: (a) does subtreeSpec live in the library (a HierarchicalSubtreeSpecFactory in spring-data) or app-side; (b) how allowed-subtree-roots are computed (which ancestor grants the subject holds that are inheritable to the listed type) without a per-row resolve; (c) deny-overrides on lists (a denied leaf must drop out even if a subtree grant would include it); (d) the e2e shape (two subjects, same list endpoint, different subtree row sets + a denied carve-out). Per-node independent grants remain Phase 8 (ReBAC). PROCESS: the established slice ritual — grill-me if useful, an ADR 0009 ONLY if a list-specific fork surfaces (else ADR 0008 governs), a full planning package under docs/to-do/planning/HIERARCHY-LIST-FILTER/ (the [[HIERARCHY-LIST-FILTER]] wikilink is already an intentional forward stub from the 5.5-A index), the slice-planner skill for decomposition, branch feature/void3110/hierarchy-list-filter, identity Void3110 <void31102025@gmail.com>, clean-room, Mulch sync .mulch-only.

title: Keep the tag access requirement on the RoleDefinition (AWS-IAM-style), not on the resource (Keycloak-style)
rationale: Deep-research (NIST SP 800-162, AWS IAM ABAC docs, Keycloak Authorization Services, XACML; 24/25 claims verified 3-0) confirmed both are valid ABAC but they differ decisively for THIS repo. Subject-side (today): requiredTags+matchMode live on the role; resources carry plain tag VALUES; matchMode ALL_OF/ANY_OF == AWS ForAllValues/ForAnyValue. It is FAIL-CLOSED by construction (no role def -> DENY_ALL; no requiredTags -> vacuously-true full reach; tags only SUBTRACT) and composes natively with the Phase-5 partial-eval row filter (requirement -> residual WHERE over the tags JSONB). Resource-side (Keycloak: a permission attaches policies to the protected resource) is intuitive for resource owners BUT its natural default 'untagged resource is open to everyone' is a documented FAIL-OPEN (AWS warns ForAllValues is vacuously true over an empty/absent key — the same hazard) which conflicts with the repo's load-bearing fail-closed invariant.

title: Slice 5.5-B (hierarchy-aware list filter): the 6 settled forks + ADR 0010
rationale: Planning grilled the list-specific forks ADR 0008 deferred; all pinned in ADR 0010 (the list fork is 0010, not 0009 — 0009 was taken by tag-requirement-subject-side). The 6 decisions: (1) ROOT-ONLY subtree roots — subtreeSpec = whole governing-root subtree iff the root-resolved role inheritably grants the verb, else empty; mid-tree per-node grants are Phase 8; reuses the existing root role lookup, no new 'which nodes' search. (2) SEAM = a new SubtreeSpecResolver (spring-data, owns root-resolution + inheritable gate + calls subtreeOf) feeding an ADDITIVE 4-arg AbacQueryService.findAuthorized(repo,scope,ctx,subtreeSpec) that owns scope.and(tagResidual.or(subtreeSpec)).and(notDenied); 3-arg PRESERVED byte-compatible (delegates subtreeSpec=null); AbacQueryService gains NO resolver dep on the composition path (receives a ready Specification). (3) notDenied = SQL mirror of the shipped leaf deny abac_deny==true -> the SQL predicate `abac_deny IS DISTINCT FROM true` over tags JSONB, AND-ed OUTSIDE the OR (folding it inside lets the subtree branch re-admit a denied row); absent tag -> not denied (matches Rego); future non-scalar deny -> route to allowlist batch (documented, not built). (4) NEW additive SPI method AncestorResolver.subtreeOf(rootType,rootId) -> Specification (NOT Set<id>, to keep the ltree pushdown + strategy behind the SPI): ltree -> path <@ <root-label> SQL pushdown (id set never materialized); CTE -> id IN (descendants) downward walk BOUNDED by maxDepth, FAIL-CLOSED to always-false on breach/cycle/error. (5) The !fullySupported allowlist BATCH path becomes hierarchy-aware: batchFilter/withResource build per-row AbacContext WITH the row's ancestor chain (4-arg Resource) so allowAll decides each row by the same Rego final_allow as the single-GET; subtreeSpec applies to the PURE-SQL path ONLY; adds an AncestorResolver dep to the batch path (constructor change = build-breaker, update all sites same commit); cheap (ltree path already loaded). (6) ONE slice, 6 tickets (T1 subtreeOf SPI+both impls+ITs; T2 SubtreeSpecResolver; T3 4-arg overload+notDenied+batch; T4 IT no-leak+re-parent-on-list; T5 starter+example adoption; T6 e2e+docs), not split — the widening + the deny narrowing are one atomic correctness unit. FAIL-CLOSED everywhere: failed subtree resolution -> narrower tag-only (never wider); subtreeSpec OR-ed INSIDE scope.and (never escapes scope); opa-abac-core NOT touched; residual/operator-set/RoleDefinition unchanged. The recurring autonomous-run pause class (a fail-open/contract semantic left unpinned) is pre-empted: root-only, notDenied-outside-OR, batch-carries-ancestors, subtreeOf-fail-closed are all pinned in advance.

name: subtreeOf SPI: fail-closed subtree predicate (ltree ltree_isparent pushdown vs CTE bounded id-IN)
description: The inverse of the ancestor walk for hierarchy-aware LIST filtering (Slice 5.5-B): AncestorResolver.subtreeOf(rootType,rootId) returns a JPA Specification selecting a root's subtree (root-inclusive), to be OR-ed into a list query. TWO impls, strategy behind the SPI. ltree: ltree_isparent(rootPath, entity.path) — the FUNCTION FORM of the @> operator (reverse of <@), so the predicate stays in JPA Criteria (cb.function, no native-SQL operator string); the bound root path is cast via text2ltree(?); the descendant id set is NEVER materialized in Java. CTE: a downward parent_id walk (a new optional DescendantIdSource SPI, childrenOf -> List<ParentRef> carrying types so the walk recurses) materializes the bounded descendant id set -> id IN (...). KEY: unlike ancestorsOf (which THROWS fail-closed), subtreeOf SWALLOWS to an always-false predicate (cb.disjunction()) on any breach/error/missing-source — because it is OR-ed into a query, a no-op widening is the safe collapse, never wider. maxDepth-bounded + cycle-guarded; both impls implement it additively; opa-abac-core untouched.

A JPA Criteria 'id IN (...)' predicate built from STRING ids fails against a Postgres uuid column with: ERROR operator does not exist: uuid = character varying. root.get("id").as(String.class).in(stringIds) does NOT cast the column in SQL — it binds varchar literals against the uuid column. Surfaced in the CTE subtreeOf id-IN path (Slice 5.5-B T1) where descendant ids flow through the type-agnostic AncestorResolver SPI as strings.
resolution: Bind the ids as the entity id column's actual type: convert each string id to java.util.UUID when it parses as one (else keep verbatim), so root.get("id").in(uuidList) binds uuid literals. This is the column-type-agreement analogue of the residual's scalar-vs-array care (mx-6876cd). The base entities (BaseModel) all use UUID ids.

name: SubtreeSpecResolver: root-only inheritable gate mirroring the Rego inherited_grant for list widening
description: The 'whether to widen' half of the hierarchy-aware list filter (5.5-B T2). SubtreeSpecResolver(subject, childType, governingRoot, verb) -> Optional<Specification>: (1) inheritable-relation gate FIRST — childType must declare governingRoot.type inheritable (a plain childType->[ancestorType] Map, opt-in default-off), checked BEFORE any lookup so a non-inheritable list never hits the supplier; (2) resolve the role ONCE on the governing root (never per-ancestor — root-only, per-node is Phase 8); (3) verb gate verb in permissions[governingRoot.type]; grant -> Optional.of(subtreeOf(root)), else/any-exception -> Optional.empty(). CRITICAL correctness: the inheritable grant lives in permissions[ANCESTOR/root type], NOT permissions[child type] — mirrors category.rego inherited_grant (data.<t>.inheritable[child][ancestor] AND verb in role.permissions[ancestor.type]). This is what makes the widened LIST and a single-GET decide the SAME rows by construction. The inheritance Map is injected as a plain Map (not OpaAbacProperties) so opa-abac-spring-data keeps NO dependency on the starter (deps flow core<-spring-data<-starter).

name: Hierarchy-aware list composition: subtreeSpec OR-ed inside scope.and, notDenied AND-ed outside; batch carries ancestors
description: AbacQueryService 4-arg findAuthorized(repo, scope, ctx, subtreeSpec) for the hierarchy-aware list filter (5.5-B T3). Pure-SQL path: combined = scope.and( tagResidual.or(subtreeSpec) ).and( notDenied ). TWO load-bearing placements: (a) subtreeSpec OR-ed INSIDE scope.and(...) so the inheritable widening can NEVER escape the caller's catalogId scope (no cross-catalog leak); (b) notDenied AND-ed OUTSIDE the OR so a leaf deny overrides BOTH the tag branch AND the subtree branch (folding deny into the OR would re-admit denied rows). notDenied() = jsonb_extract_path_text(tags,'abac_deny') IS DISTINCT FROM 'true', expressed in Criteria as (value IS NULL) OR (value <> 'true') — absent tag -> kept (matches Rego not-denied on absent key), abac_deny=true -> excluded. The allowlist-BATCH path is independently hierarchy-aware: withResource resolves each candidate's ancestors and builds the 4-arg Resource(...,ancestors) so allowAll runs the SAME final_allow=(direct OR inherited) AND NOT denied as a single-GET; subtreeSpec is NOT applied on the batch path (redundant). The 3-arg findAuthorized stays byte-compatible (delegates with subtreeSpec=null); the new AncestorResolver ctor arg is NULLABLE (hierarchy off -> tag-only batch, fail-closed) so the always-on AbacQueryService bean wires whether or not a resolver bean exists (ObjectProvider). Fail-closed everywhere: failed subtree resolution -> narrower tag-only; batch per-row resolution failure -> empty ancestors -> direct-only; short/all-false allowAll drops rows; opa-abac-core untouched.

Two @DataJpaTest ITs in the same package each declaring their own static @SpringBootApplication TestApp -> a THIRD one added in 5.5-B made @DataJpaTest's package auto-scan fail with 'Found multiple @SpringBootConfiguration annotated classes'. Surfaces ONLY when the full module suite runs (each IT passes in isolation), so a per-test run hides it — the ★ gate's full-suite run is what caught it. Also: a subtreeOf-based list IT came back empty because the test's LtreePathSource looked the ROOT's path up in the listed table (which holds only the child rows), but subtreeOf needs the ROOT's path and the root lives in another table.
resolution: Pin EVERY @DataJpaTest IT in a shared package to its own config via @ContextConfiguration(classes = <ThatIT>.TestApp.class) — this disables the ambiguous package scan. And: subtreeOf reads the ROOT's path from wherever the root lives; in a single-table test, the LtreePathSource must SYNTHESIZE a non-listed root's path from its label (e.g. catalog_<id>), mirroring the real per-table layout where each type has its own path column. Always run the FULL module suite at the ★ gate, never just the new test.

name: Starter wiring + example adoption for the hierarchy-aware list resolver (SubtreeSpecResolver bean + 4-arg call via ObjectProvider)
description: Wire the 5.5-B list widening as a TWO-PART opt-in mirroring 5.5-A. STARTER: a SubtreeSpecResolver @Bean in HierarchyAutoConfiguration, gated @ConditionalOnBean(AncestorResolver.class) + the existing hierarchy.enabled=true (so it follows the same default-off posture and only wires when an app supplied a data-access source bean), and @ConditionalOnMissingBean (overridable). It reuses the SAME AncestorResolver + RoleDefinitionSupplier as HierarchicalAuthorizer + the inheritance map from properties.getHierarchy().getInheritable() — NO new property. EXAMPLE: the list authorizer injects ObjectProvider<SubtreeSpecResolver> (present only when hierarchy is on) and per-call resolves the subtreeSpec on the SAME governing root the role is resolved on, passing it into the 4-arg findAuthorized; absent provider / no inheritable grant -> null -> the tag-only 3-arg behavior. The always-on AbacQueryService bean injects ObjectProvider<AncestorResolver> for the batch path. SCOPE NOTE recorded: a list endpoint that does NOT already use the Phase-5 AbacQueryService partial-eval path (e.g. a plain repo.findByX scoped query) cannot be widened by subtreeSpec without FIRST adopting the Phase-5 residual filter — so adopting hierarchy on such a list is a larger, separate change, not part of this slice. ddl-auto:validate boot is the proof of no schema change.

name: Coarse list-gate rego clause: open the type-level @OpaPreAuthorize gate for an inheritable ancestor grant on a LIST
description: Slice 5.5-B's one design fork the planning didn't pin (settled with the maintainer). The type-level @OpaPreAuthorize(<type>:read) on a LIST endpoint evaluates  with only a resource TYPE (no id, no ancestors), so inherited_grant (which needs ancestors) can't fire -> a subject whose role grants read ONLY on an inheritable ancestor (e.g. {catalog:[read]}) — the very subject the subtreeSpec widening exists for — is denied 403 at the COARSE gate before the SQL widening runs (opa eval confirms allow=false). FIX: a small ADDITIVE second `allow` clause: allow if { not input.resource.id ; not denied ; list_inheritable_grant } where list_inheritable_grant if { some ancestor_type,_ in data.category.inheritable[input.resource.type] ; verb in input.role_definition.permissions[ancestor_type] }. It ONLY opens the coarse 'may you read <type> at all' gate; the FINE which-rows cut still happens in SQL (the app-built subtreeSpec). Scoped to a LIST via  so single-resource decisions are byte-unchanged (a dedicated opa-test pins this); AND-s ; opt-in/default-off via the same data.<pkg>.inheritable 5.5-A ships (NO new data); a stranger with no role_definition can't pass. PLANNING FEEDBACK: a list-WIDENING slice must ALSO open the coarse list gate for inheritable grants, or the e2e 403s before the widening. Proven by run-hierarchy-list-matrix.sh through the gateway (10/10) + 5 new opa tests (77/77).

title: NEXT: Phase 5.9 REST API refinement (publication-readiness) BEFORE Phase 6 action enrichment
rationale: Slice 5.5-B (hierarchy-aware list filter) is SHIPPED + MERGED to main (PR #21; Phase 5.5 complete: 5.5-A single-resource + 5.5-B list filter). The maintainer chose to insert a REST API refinement step BEFORE action enrichment, driven by docs/code-review/REST-API-DESIGN-REVIEW.md. That review found the API is sound and consistent with NO fail-open; the gaps are maturity/publication-readiness items. SCOPE (the review's priority-ordered follow-ups): (1) MEDIUM the publication item: RFC-7807 application/problem+json + a machine-stable errorCode enum so clients branch on a code not a localizable message (currently ApiError{status,message,timestamp} as application/json); (2) LOW Location header on every 201 (the id is already known); (3) LOW-MEDIUM one-line 'bootstrap: pre-membership, authenticated-only by design' intent comments at the deliberately-ungated user-service mutations (UserController, POST /teams) so an absent @OpaPreAuthorize reads as a decision; (4) DEFERRED a shared pagination envelope (a library-wide slice when volume justifies, NOT per-endpoint); (5) Phase-6 the actions/pageActions affordance metadata stays action-enrichment. Sequenced before Phase 6 so the _actions envelope lands on an already-RFC-7807-clean surface. Added to POC-ROADMAP as Phase 5.9. NEXT ACTION when work resumes: run the planning ritual — grill-me to settle the slice scope (how far to take problem+json; pagination in or deferred), then an ADR for the error-contract decision, then the slice-planner decomposition package, mirroring how 5.5-B was planned. The guide to refine against is docs/guides/REST-API-DESIGN.md (§3 status codes, §9 targets).

description: Testcontainers ITs failed with 'Could not find a valid Docker environment' even though podman machine reported running. Root cause: the podman machine claimed State=running but its API socket file (ConnectionInfo.PodmanSocket.Path under TMPDIR) was MISSING (stale machine state), so the build's resolveDockerHost() (which checks file(path).exists()) returned null and Testcontainers fell back to default strategies that probe /var/run/docker.sock (a dead symlink to the absent podman sock) and the Docker Desktop CLI socket (not a usable API socket) — both fail. Exporting DOCKER_HOST in the shell does NOT help because the Gradle test worker fork does not inherit it and the build only injects DOCKER_HOST when resolveDockerHost() is non-null. ~/.testcontainers.properties docker.host was also not honored by the failing strategy order.
resolution: Restart the podman machine: podman machine stop then podman machine start. This recreates the API socket (start prints 'API forwarding listening on: /var/run/docker.sock'). Then resolveDockerHost() finds the socket via podman machine inspect and the build auto-injects DOCKER_HOST into the test task as designed. Environment fix, no code change. If podman is genuinely unavailable, point DOCKER_HOST at the Docker Desktop RAW socket (~/.docker/run/docker.sock, NOT the docker-cli.sock) so the build's priority-1 env branch fires.

description: Phase 5.9 e2e: the tag and team newman matrices failed on user-service endpoints (a define-tag 201 had no Location; a gated 403 returned application/json not application/problem+json) even after running ./deploy.sh build and redeploying. Root cause: ./deploy.sh build rebuilds ONLY the catalog app image (build_image). The user-management image (opa-abac-usermgmt:local) is rebuilt ONLY by build_usermgmt_image, which deploy.sh invokes lazily as 'usermgmt_image_exists || build_usermgmt_image' inside the up path — so when a stale usermgmt image already exists, NEITHER deploy.sh build NOR deploy.sh up rebuilds it. The pod therefore kept serving 6-day-old code (the legacy ApiError body, no Location). Catalog-side assertions passed because the catalog image WAS rebuilt; only the user-service-routed requests failed.
resolution: When a slice changes user-service code, force its image explicitly: docker build -t opa-abac-usermgmt:local -f example-user-management-service/Dockerfile . (build context is the repo ROOT for the multi-module Gradle build), then recreate the container: docker compose -p opa-abac-example -f infra/compose.usermgmt.yaml up -d --force-recreate, and wait for http://localhost:28090/actuator/health UP. Symptom signature: in a two-service e2e, contract assertions pass on catalog routes but fail on user-service routes with the OLD body shape -> suspect a stale usermgmt image, not a code bug. (Consider teaching deploy.sh build to also rebuild usermgmt when ENABLE_USER_SERVICE=1.)

title: Default JWT extractor requires explicit trust-forwarded-jwt opt-in
rationale: JwtClaimsSubjectExtractor verifies no signature by design (gateway-trust). Documented-but-unguarded meant a gateway-less deployment silently accepted self-minted tokens — total auth bypass. The starter now wires a refusing extractor (anonymous → deny + startup WARN) until opa.abac.subject.trust-forwarded-jwt=true; an app-supplied AbacSubjectExtractor bean bypasses the toggle. The dead verify-signature no-op property was removed (a security-named toggle that does nothing invites false safety). Rule: a dangerous default must be an explicit opt-in property, not a javadoc warning.

description: E2E hierarchy matrix failed only on a long-lived rig: its 'foreign' catalog fixture id (4444) is the hierarchy-LIST matrix's GRANTED root, and the user-service DB persists across runs — a stale team from a past list-matrix run granted the same viewer reader an inheritable role on 4444, flipping the re-parent 403 assert into a policy-correct 200. Looked exactly like a library regression after a redeploy; the library was right, the fixtures were poisoned.
resolution: Fixture-id discipline across matrices: an id one matrix uses as a NEGATIVE case must never be an id another matrix GRANTS on (registry now in scripts/postman/README.md; hierarchy-foreign moved to 6666). When an e2e negative-case assert fails on a long-lived rig, check the persistent usermgmt teams for stale grants on the fixture id BEFORE suspecting the code: SELECT ... FROM team WHERE target_id LIKE '<id-prefix>%'.

title: Phase-③ stays bare-prompt for single-repo slices; phase-② gates are committed scripts
rationale: All 8 shipped slices were single-repo with no resume/re-entry need; the AUTONOMOUS-IMPLEMENT-SKILL-TEMPLATE's own guidance says the skill wrapper only earns its keep for multi-repo, resume-heavy, or enforced-escalation slices. Deterministic committed scripts beat prose gates (code is deterministic; language interpretation is not).

title: Sub-agents scout and validate; the implementer implements (autonomous-run delegation policy)
rationale: Decided with the maintainer 2026-06-11 (Phase 5.95 planning), pinned in AUTONOMOUS-IMPLEMENTATION-FLOW.md (the section-4 template line + a section-7 rationale bullet + an operator-note bullet). The per-ticket implementation stays in the main loop: across 8 shipped runs the failure modes were unpinned design semantics and rig gotchas, never context exhaustion, while cross-ticket continuity (T1 micro-decisions shaping later tickets) is what keeps a run coherent; per-ticket sub-agents re-read the whole package + re-prime Mulch each time (similar token cost) and drift at every seam. ALLOWED delegation: read-only scouting fan-outs (e.g. 'which collections assert list bodies') and log-noisy validation (run newman/build, return only the failure summary). Context pressure is handled by stopping at a checkpoint and resuming in a FRESH SESSION - the ticket status table + STATUS-0N notes are a complete handoff (the method is doc-first so the window is cache, not the source of truth).

description: e2e runner seeds a catalog row via direct SQL without the ltree path column -> the first category creation under it dies 500 with AncestorResolutionException 'parent has no path (broken lineage)' (HierarchicalPathMaintainer fail-closes on NULL parent path, by design since 5.5-A). Pre-5.5-A fixture rows were backfilled by the adoption migration, so OLD matrices never trip this — only NEW direct-SQL seeds do (discovered in the 5.95 pagination matrix). The json_field id extraction then KeyErrors under set -euo pipefail before the friendly error prints, so the symptom is a bare python Traceback.
resolution: Seed catalogs the run-hierarchy-matrix.sh way: INSERT ... (tags, path) VALUES (..., CAST('catalog_' || replace('<uuid>','-','') AS ltree)) and make the conflict arm repair it too: ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET name = EXCLUDED.name, path = EXCLUDED.path (a prior failed run leaves a NULL-path row behind). CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS ltree first.

name: Paged findAuthorized: guard + four paths + PageImpl over the filtered fallback (exact subject-relative count)
description: Paginate an ABAC-filtered list by an ADDITIVE Pageable overload on the query seam (5.95): findAuthorized(repo, scope, ctx, subtreeSpec, Pageable) -> Page<T>. (1) Guard FIRST: pageable.getSort().isUnsorted() -> IllegalArgumentException before any OPA/repo call — pagination without a total order silently repeats/drops rows; services pass a fixed createdAt ASC, id ASC (id tiebreaker = total order). (2) Pure-SQL: the IDENTICAL scope.and(tagResidual.or(subtreeSpec)).and(notDenied) composition paged — extract it to ONE private helper shared by the unpaged and paged paths so they cannot drift. (3) Allowlist fallback: fetch candidates SQL-SORTED with pageable.getSort() (path-independent order vs pure-SQL), batchFilter unchanged (order-preserving), slice the window in memory -> new PageImpl(slice, pageable, survivors.size()) — the survivor count IS the exact count; zero new cost (the path is fetch-all already). (4) Kill-switch: coarse allow then scope.and(notDenied) paged. (5) fromError: Page.empty(pageable), NO repo call — a failed compile empties the page INCLUDING the count (no count leak), and never triggers the fallback. totalElements is the subject-relative authorized total on every path — never items.length. Decisive IT: two subjects 5-vs-3 totals; a perPage=2 walk == the single-page list element-for-element; fallback pages byte-identical to pure-SQL pages.

name: Suite-wide wire-shape break in newman: scout the blast radius, migrate extraction only, keep every pinned count
description: Migrating every list response from bare array to an envelope across a newman suite (5.95): (1) SCOUT first (a read-only sub-agent sweep): find every test-script line treating a list body as an array (json.map/.length/[0]/Array.isArray + variables storing list bodies) — the 5.95 sweep found only 3 of 7 collections consumed list bodies (8 sites), the rest asserted status only; (2) migrate ONLY the extraction (pm.response.json().map -> pm.response.json().items.map) and keep every pinned numeric expectation numerically identical (1/1/>=3/0) — the cut must not move, only the shape; (3) give the new matrix a DEDICATED fixture set in the fixture-id registry (7777…) because its counts are pinned exactly (5/3) and shared fixtures must not grow; (4) seed catalogs in runner SQL WITH the ltree path (and repair it in the ON CONFLICT arm) — see the broken-lineage failure record. Validation: a sub-agent runs all runners sequentially and reports only failure summaries (8 scripts, 128 assertions).

title: 5.97 decomposition pinned two contract semantics the design left implicit (missing-id 403; conjunct over scope-out)
rationale: Decomposing RESOURCE-RESOLUTION surfaced two externally-visible semantics ADR 0013 implied but never stated, and pinned them in 01-DECOMPOSITION so the autonomous run never stops to ask: (1) ADR 0013's 'resolver empty/throws -> DENY' read literally means a MISSING id behind an annotated resourceId answers 403 where it answered 404 pre-5.97 (the gate denies before the handler can 404); wrong-scope-but-existing stays the handler's 404. Consequence found at decompose time: the catalog CRUD ITs must run with opa.abac.resource-resolution.enabled=false (they test CRUD, not authz) and double as the kill-switch off-state proof, while a new ResourceResolutionGateIT owns the gate cells - otherwise every missing-id IT/e2e cell flips red mid-run. (2) The retro-audit fold-in offered 'tags_satisfied conjunct OR documented category-only scope' for product/catalog.rego; the package picks the conjunct (mirror category.rego verbatim, vacuous back-compat) per the audit's security-first disposition. Both flagged for maintainer review of the package. The general lesson: a fail-closed rule at the GATE re-types not-found from 404 to 403 on every annotated id'd endpoint - any slice that moves a decision earlier in the request lifecycle must sweep the status-code contract of the paths it now preempts.

name: Starter-shipped @RestControllerAdvice must be standalone, never a subclass of the shared advice base
description: When a starter auto-registers an exception-mapping @RestControllerAdvice (e.g. PersistenceConflictProblemAdvice mapping OptimisticLockingFailureException/DataIntegrityViolationException -> 409 STATE_CONFLICT problem+json), do NOT extend the shared AbstractProblemAdvice base the applications also extend: the subclass would inherit the base's @ExceptionHandler methods (AccessDeniedException etc.), and cross-advice handler resolution in ExceptionHandlerExceptionResolver is order-dependent — the starter's inherited handler could silently shadow (or be shadowed by) every service's own advice for those exceptions. Standalone advice + its own ProblemDetailFactory produces the identical body shape with zero ambiguity; @ConditionalOnClass(name=...) string-guards the dao types for non-JPA adopters, @ConditionalOnMissingBean keeps it overridable. Same body shape, disjoint handler sets.

name: Deterministic TOCTOU race ITs: two aspect hooks pin the gate-window guard AND the post-guard @Version backstop
description: To prove version-binding 409 contracts deterministically (no sleeps/threads), register a test @Aspect with two get-and-clear AtomicReference<Runnable> hooks: (1) BEFORE_HANDLER on the controller method — an unordered aspect is LOWEST_PRECEDENCE so it runs INSIDE the order-190 method-security interceptor, i.e. after the gate decided+cached and before the handler loads: a JDBC version-bump here must trip the VersionGuard (gate snapshot != fresh load -> 409, mutation not applied); (2) BEFORE_SAVE on the repository save (pointcut: this(XRepository) && execution(* save(..))) — fires after the handler's load+guard, so a bump here forces a stale-@Version merge -> OptimisticLockingFailureException -> the starter's 409 advice (proving the post-guard backstop live, not 500). Together the two hooks cover every gate->write window. Bumps via JdbcTemplate auto-commit so the racing write is visible to the handler's transaction. Gotcha: if the schema's FKs are all ON DELETE CASCADE there is no natural DataIntegrityViolation to test the advice with — the stale-save route is the deterministic alternative.

A new e2e matrix runner seeded its fixture catalog row via psql without the ltree path column (modeled on run-tag-matrix.sh) and every gateway category create under it failed 500 fail-closed: 'cannot assign path: parent catalog:<id> has no path (broken lineage)'. run-tag-matrix.sh's pathless INSERT only appears to work because the postgres volume persists across sessions and its row already carries a path from an earlier run — on a fresh volume it would fail the same way.
resolution: Seed fixture catalog rows WITH the path (the run-pagination-matrix.sh model): INSERT ... path = CAST('catalog_' || replace('<id>','-','') AS ltree), and let the ON CONFLICT arm repair path = EXCLUDED.path for rows a prior run left NULL. Any direct-SQL row for a hierarchical type must carry its materialized path.

name: Gate-side resource resolution: split SPI + governing-root role + write-through request cache (ADR 0013 shape)
description: To make an annotation-driven pre-authorization gate decide on a resource's REAL attributes instead of a bare (type,id) reference: (1) one app-implemented AbacResourceResolver bean (Optional<AbacDataObject> resolve(type,id), dispatching internally) + a separate core AncestorChainSupplier the STARTER binds to the hierarchy resolver — the security module never sees data-module types; (2) the manager gains a constructor overload taking a ResourceResolutionSupport composition (resolver + nullable chainSupplier + cache); support absent => byte-identical baseline (pin with a serialized-context golden string test); (3) the role is resolved ONCE on the governing root (ancestors.isEmpty() ? leaf : ancestors.get(0)) so the gate decision equals the layer-3 decision it replaces; (4) split failure semantics, never confused: instance empty/throw -> DENY with no OPA call (an attribute-less context would WIDEN past attribute-keyed deny rules); ancestor throw -> collapse to empty chain, direct-only (never strips a direct grant); (5) the request-attributes cache is write-through on allow ONLY and never read by decisions — handlers reuse the authorized snapshot, decisions always resolve fresh; (6) a kill-switch property (default on, matchIfMissing) restores baseline semantics with beans untouched. Under an HTTP role source with exact target matching, the governing-root lookup is what closes the tag-blind realm-fallback hole on id'd member decisions.

name: Version binding: gate snapshot guarded against the fresh load via the one JPA @Version -> 409
description: Binding an authorization decision to the state a mutation acts on, without persisting the decision snapshot: reads return the cached authorized snapshot (the response IS the state the decision saw); mutating handlers load fresh in-transaction as always, then VersionGuard.requireUnchanged(snapshot, fresh) BEFORE any write — drift OR a null version throws VersionConflictException (fail loud, one exception type keeps the advice mapping total) -> 409 STATE_CONFLICT problem+json with a STATIC detail; the client re-reads and retries and the retry's gate decides on the new state. The one existing JPA @Version is the version (an ABAC-only counter is a silent-fail-open trap). Layered windows: gate->handler-load is the guard's (deterministic IT via a pre-handler aspect bump); post-guard belongs to @Version + the starter's dao advice (deterministic IT via a pre-save bump). Where a pessimistic lock exists (mutate(id, fn)), guard INSIDE the locked tx against the locked row — decide under the protection you act under.

title: Missing id behind an annotated resourceId answers 403 (gate deny), wrong-scope-but-existing keeps the handler's 404
rationale: ADR 0013's literal fail-closed rule (resolver empty/throws -> DENY) re-types not-found from 404 to 403 on every annotated id'd endpoint once a resolver is registered — pinned as anti-enumeration posture rather than special-cased, because any 'empty -> let the handler 404' carve-out would rebuild the attribute-less context path the rule exists to forbid. The 403/404 split is NOT an existence oracle: the wrong-scope 404 is only reachable by callers the policy already ALLOWED for the resource. Operationally: CRUD/error-contract ITs run on the kill-switch off-profile (doubling as the baseline proof); exactly one e2e cell suite-wide (catalog-e2e get-after-delete) flipped 404->403 and was re-pinned in place. General lesson: a slice that moves a decision earlier in the request lifecycle must sweep the status-code contract of every path it now preempts.

name: Commit-time constraint violations dodge the 409 advice: flush inside the @Transactional method
description: A DataIntegrityViolationException raised at TRANSACTION COMMIT (the default flush point) surfaces from the @Transactional proxy as an untranslated wrapper (e.g. TransactionSystemException) that a @RestControllerAdvice @ExceptionHandler(DataIntegrityViolationException) never catches -> the FK conflict answers 500 even though the advice exists. The deterministic fix: repository.flush() INSIDE the transactional service method right after the violating write (e.g. roles.delete(role); roles.flush()), so Spring's exception translation runs in-method and the typed exception propagates to the advice -> 409 STATE_CONFLICT. Found wiring the in-use-role-delete 409 (retro-audit follow-up); the 5.97 starter advice alone was NOT sufficient without the in-method flush. Pinned by ErrorContractIT.deletingAnInUseCustomRoleIsProblemJsonWithStateConflict.

After Phase 5.97 moved id'd decisions to the gate (role resolved on the GOVERNING ROOT; role-def ABSENT at the root -> the realm fallback decides, the pinned E4 semantic), the hierarchy matrix's re-parent flip cell -- written in 5.5-A when layer-3 HierarchicalAuthorizer denied role-less reads outright -- started legitimately answering 200 for a realm-viewer on a team-less foreign root. The 403 it asserted had been produced by a deny MECHANISM the slice replaced, not by the semantics it claimed to pin. A stale mechanism hides behind a green assert until the rig is rebuilt.
resolution: Make the negative cell role-DRIVEN: bind the reader to a deliberate no-grant role (permissions {}) on a team governing the foreign root, so role-def-present disables the fallback (the E3 semantic) and the flip stays provable for the right reason (run-hierarchy-matrix.sh, fixed on the audit-followups-hardening branch). Rule for future slices that change WHO/WHERE a deny comes from: sweep every negative e2e cell and ask 'which mechanism produces this 4xx today?'

description: The example services' OpenAPI ProblemDetail.errorCode is a CLOSED enum ('the union of codes this service can emit'). When the starter's PersistenceConflictProblemAdvice started emitting STATE_CONFLICT (5.97), neither catalog-api.yaml nor user-mgmt-api.yaml gained the value -- the catalog under-documented its I4/I5 409s for a whole slice, and the audit-followups branch made the same code reachable in user-mgmt (in-use-role-delete) without touching the spec. A generated client deserializing into the closed enum fails on the undeclared value. Found by the deep-review api-contract lens; the catalog mirror only by the completeness critic (a per-file lens is structurally blind to the sibling spec).
resolution: Both enums extended with STATE_CONFLICT (audit-followups-hardening branch). Rule: whenever a starter advice or handler starts emitting a LibraryErrorCode on a service's wire, grep BOTH specs' errorCode enums in the same commit -- the enum is part of the error contract, and 'reachable but undeclared' survives green builds because nothing validates emitted codes against the spec.

title: Phase 6.5 permission categories: the ten pinned forks
rationale: Clean cut: zero external adopters makes back-compat machinery pure cost (legacy aliases would live in the expansion table forever and publish dirty). Hybrid gates: the team-row lock and decide-under-protection live in Java (B3), while the expansion table must stay editable-without-redeploy in OPA data — splitting the gates along that line keeps one runtime source for effective_actions with no TOCTOU. Deferring define-tags keeps the Q1 scope boundary honest (the dictionary endpoints are control-plane-gated) and avoids a silent default widening (member ceiling includes TAG).

title: 6.5 decomposition pinned five contract semantics the design left implicit
rationale: The recurring planning-gap class is 'an externally-visible semantic left unpinned pauses the run' (mx-7e0a17); decomposing PERMISSION-CATEGORIES surfaced five and pinned them in 01-DECOMPOSITION's preamble rather than mid-run: (1) authoring violations -> 422 with NEW UserMgmtErrorCode ROLE_DEFINITION_INVALID + the closed OpenAPI errorCode enum swept in the same commit, while ALL assignment-gate rejections (level, senior bound, assignable subset, AND an OPA outage during the verdict) keep the one existing 422 ROLE_SUBSET_VIOLATION shape - outage deliberately indistinguishable from not-assignable (fail-closed by indistinguishability); (2) the pinned TAG-without-WRITE-can-relabel cell is unreachable with a static @OpaPreAuthorize on PUT, so update endpoints move to delta-aware dispatch via an annotated gate bean (content->update, tags->assign-tags, both->both, empty->update conservative) - manager seam + 5.97 cache reused, zero library change; (3) the nine-runner payload migration is a mechanical rule (read->[READ], read+write->[READ,WRITE,TAG] because pre-6.5 write implied tag-setting - same principle as the realm-fallback mapping; +roleLevel 10/20) that must preserve every pinned cell; (4) the stale-flat-role e2e cell seeds via direct DB INSERT because the authoring API now rejects flat tokens by design; (5) missing/non-numeric role_level on either assignment snapshot rejects, never 0-and-pass.

name: PE-inline idiom: partial-eval filter rules must consume data tables inline, never via user functions
description: OPA's partial evaluator does NOT inline user functions over an unknown argument: a filter rule written as 'verb in permissions.effective_actions(input.role_definition, input.resource.type)' leaves data.permissions.tokens_for(...) calls and set comprehensions in the residual, which CompileResponseParser rejects (unsupported -> batch fallback for EVERY list). The working idiom: consume the SAME data table through a positive inline membership chain ('some token in perms[input.resource.type]; "list" in data.permission_categories[token]') - the known role + known table fold completely, leaving only the type-eq tautology + tag conditions (the 5.x residual shape). One expansion home (data.permission_categories), two consumption idioms: function for full eval (allow/assignable), inline chain for PE. Negation over an unknown-keyed lookup ('not denied[input.resource.type]') folds ONLY when the map is empty; a denial-carrying role degrades to unsupported -> batch recheck via allow (fail-closed, never widens). Verify residual shapes EMPIRICALLY with 'opa eval --partial' before committing to a formulation.

Liquibase sql changesets that use Postgres jsonb operators containing '?' (jsonb_exists ?, ?| , ?&) fail at migration time with 'syntax error at or near $1' - the JDBC driver rewrites every ? as a bind-parameter placeholder before Postgres sees it. Surfaced in the 6.5 seed-sweep changeset (0006-permission-categories.yaml) where 'e.value ? ''read''' broke every Testcontainers IT boot.
resolution: Use the function forms instead of the operators in any SQL that flows through JDBC/Liquibase: jsonb_exists(col, 'key') for ?, jsonb_exists_any for ?|, jsonb_exists_all for ?&. Same semantics, no placeholder collision.

name: Hybrid assignment gates: Java tier compares under the row lock + an app-side OPA entrypoint client, fail-closed
description: The 6.5 delegation shape: assignment authority = (1) a Java cross-tier level compare (actorLevel > candidateLevel from attributes.role_level; unreadable level REJECTS, never 0-and-pass) + (2) at the senior tier only, an OPA subset-on-effective verdict (data.role.assignable over RAW row snapshots - the policy's shared effective_actions does wildcard+denial math, so Java never reimplements set algebra). Both gates and snapshots read AFTER lockTeam in the same tx (decide-under-protection; latch IT proves the stale snapshot would have passed). The OPA call needs an app-side RestClient (OpaClient exposes no arbitrary entrypoint): short timeouts, any error/non-2xx/missing result -> false. Level gates run FIRST so the verdict is never consulted when the tier already rejects (ITs assert zero stub calls via a counting in-process HttpServer). Gotcha pair: (a) a custom role at an admin/senior LEVEL has the authoring ceiling but NO live manage capability (TeamRoleCapabilities keys by CODE) - tier-with-denial cells are only constructible at service level; (b) a TOCTOU latch cell must pick tiers where the STALE snapshot passes, or the outcome cannot distinguish stale-read from lock-read.

name: Delta-aware gate dispatch: conditional decisions via an annotated gate bean, reachability-scoped
description: To enforce a TAG/WRITE-style boundary that a static @OpaPreAuthorize cannot express (TAG-without-WRITE relabels but never edits), move the update handler's authorization to CONDITIONAL calls on a dedicated gate bean whose methods each carry their own @OpaPreAuthorize (manager seam + 5.97 request cache reused; calls must cross the bean boundary - never self-invocation). Dispatch: content delta -> :update; tags delta (RAW request map vs entity tags, null=empty, clearing counts - raw compare can only OVER-ask) -> :assign-tags; both -> both; EMPTY delta -> :update (conservative). Decisions precede the version guard, the tag validation (no 422-vocabulary leak to unauthorized callers), and any mutation. THREE knock-ons to plan for: (1) scope the dispatch to types whose REST requests actually carry tags - an unreachable assign-tags branch is dead code; (2) the handler's missing-id answer flips 403->404 (the annotated-resourceId precondition moves off the handler; the load precedes the dispatch); (3) any aspect-injected gate-window race IT pinned on that handler loses its window - move the cell to a still-statically-annotated sibling.

6.5 e2e (E1b): a deny-overrides cell flipped (DELETE 204 instead of 403) because the fixture role granted WRITE on the CATALOG as well as the category - inherited_grant consults the ANCESTOR type's effective set, where delete was not denied, so the category-type denial was bypassed via the 5.5-A inheritance path. This is the DESIGNED semantic (00-DESIGN 2.9: per-type subtraction; effective_actions(role, ancestor_type) on the inherited path), not a policy bug.
resolution: Denials are PER TYPE and do not veto other grant paths: to fence an action subtree-wide, deny it on EVERY granted type or use a wildcard denial key '*' (denied_for is wildcard-aware). When writing deny-overrides fixtures/cells, grant the category-bearing type ONLY what the cell needs - an ancestor-type WRITE legitimately covers subtree actions. Documented in the PERMISSION-MODEL guide (T8) as the adopter-facing subtlety.

description: A permission-vocabulary migration swept only the annotation strings: T6 migrated every @OpaPreAuthorize action but missed the two Java components that EMIT or CONSUME the old tokens — DemoRoleDefinitionSupplier (still emitted flat read/write; the default demo profile denied everything under the 6.5 policies via the clean-cut ∅-expansion) and CategoryListAuthorizer→SubtreeSpecResolver (asked for flat 'read' which no category-token role carries; the 5.5-B subtree widening went silently dead — every inheritable list degraded to the batch recheck, CORRECT rows masking the regression, so all e2e stayed green).
resolution: Deep-review fix 136e826: demo supplier now emits READ / READ+WRITE+TAG mirroring the realm fallback; the list authorizer passes the READ token behind a conservative pre-gate (no denials on the root type, no required_tags — token membership can't see either and an over-widened subtreeSpec would LEAK rows since it is OR-ed with the residual); CategoryListWideningParityTest pins 'list expands from READ and only READ' to the OPA data table. Decomposition rule for the next vocabulary change: enumerate every Java emitter/consumer of the old vocabulary (suppliers, authorizers, capability maps, resolver verbs), grep-derived, in the ticket itself — annotation sweeps are not enough, and a fail-closed degrade can hide the miss behind green tests.

name: Target-tier gate: every grant gate needs its revoke/demote mirror
description: Phase 6.5's hybrid gates bounded only the role being GRANTED (actor > candidate, senior subset verdict) — and removeMember took no actor at all. Pre-6.5 unreachable (every manage holder sat at/above all non-owner targets); the senior tier is the FIRST below-tier manage holder, making 'senior demotes/removes an administrator' a live escalation (deep-review Critical, fixed in 136e826). The gate: acting ON an existing member (changeRole/removeMember) rejects when the target's CURRENT role_level is strictly above the actor's (422 ROLE_SUBSET_VIOLATION). Pinned semantics: peers stay manageable (admin removes a peer admin — the pre-6.5 cell, preserved); an unreadable TARGET level never outranks (revocation only NARROWS access, and a member holding a corrupted role must stay removable — the deliberate asymmetry with the strict actor-side levelOf); DELETE resolves the actor from the authenticated subject (no body). General rule: whenever a slice introduces a new tier or capability holder BELOW an existing tier, the revoke/demote/unassign mirror of every grant gate becomes reachable and needs its own QA row.

name: Delta-dispatched decisions must version-bind EVERY downstream mutation branch
description: The 6.5 delta dispatch decides WHICH authorization questions to ask from a pre-lock read; the no-reparent branch carried that read's @Version into save (drift -> optimistic 409), but the RE-PARENT branch replaced the entity with a fresh post-lock re-read (entityManager.clear() + findById after the native path rewrite) — absorbing any racer that committed in the window (which contains the slow tag-validation HTTP call) and silently overwriting it on the final save, including across the very WRITE/TAG boundary the dispatch decided (deep-review Critical, fixed in 136e826). Fix shape: pass the decision snapshot (the pre-dispatch entity, a Versioned) INTO the locked service; VersionGuard.requireUnchanged(snapshot, lockedRow) right after the FOR UPDATE read, before any write -> VersionConflictException -> the uniform 409 STATE_CONFLICT. Review rule: when a handler's decisions are computed on a loaded entity, trace every mutation branch downstream — any branch that re-loads (locked or not) has DISCARDED the binding unless it explicitly re-checks the decision-time version under its own protection.

title: Route to publish (settled 2026-06-13): B2 fix-slice -> 6.7 (+control-plane B2 design folds in) -> Phase 6 enrichment -> Phase 7 publish
rationale: After 6.5 merged (PR #34), the maintainer set the route to publication. SETTLED ORDER: (1) a STANDALONE B2 fix-slice FIRST — the supplier-outage error-distinct posture (resolve outage currently rides the realm fallback and, post-6.5, erases denied_actions/required_tags narrowing); fixed on its own small branch (distinguish outage->deny from no-role->fallback at the SPI contract), isolating the security fix with its own design+review rather than folding into 6.7. (2) Phase 6.7 control-plane vocabulary categorization — team:* verbs, TeamRoleCapabilities, the resolve-side team-verb injection ladder, and the define-tags ENFORCEMENT 6.5 deferred (Epic G/Story G4: ships in expansion math only today). Closes the one visible 'shipped-in-math-not-enforced' gap; the natural last correctness slice before publish. Inputs: ADR 0007 + the 6.5 addendum; PERMISSION-CATEGORIES 00-DESIGN decisions 1/5/8 (the deferred surfaces). Needs its own phase-① (escalation analysis for categorized control-plane power is a different problem from the catalog-domain taxonomy). (3) Phase 6 action enrichment — sequenced AFTER 6.7 per the maintainer (a more complete feature story before publish; affordance metadata is the portfolio/consulting differentiator); consumes 5.97 attributes + the 6.5 vocabulary, independent of 6.7. (4) Phase 7 publish prep. Small tracked items (OPA authn/trust docs, CI-runs-e2e, runner OPA-restart hygiene) fold into Phase 7 polish unless a slice touches them first. NOTE this REORDERS the roadmap's old 6->6.7 to 6.7->6.

name: B2 supplier-outage: the 5 lookup() consumers an SPI change must sweep
description: The B2 fix (distinguish resolve OUTAGE->deny from authoritative NO-ROLE->fallback) is an SPI-contract change on RoleDefinitionSupplier.lookup(). It is NOT one-file: lookup() has 5 PRODUCTION consumers, all collapsing Optional.empty() via .orElse(null) so outage==no-role today: (1) OpaPreAuthorizeAuthorizationManager:119 (spring-security), (2) OpaAuthorizationManager:69 (spring-security), (3) HierarchicalAuthorizer:85 (spring-data), (4) SubtreeSpecResolver:104 (spring-data), (5) CategoryListAuthorizer:85 (catalog example). Plus 3 implementors: NoOpRoleDefinitionSupplier, DemoRoleDefinitionSupplier, HttpRoleDefinitionSupplier (the outage source); and the user-mgmt TeamRoleDefinitionSupplier. The rego seam is has_role_definition (= input.role_definition.permissions present) gating the realm fallback in catalog/category/product.rego. Any consumer left on old semantics = silent residual widening hole. This is the PERMISSION-CATEGORIES-REVIEW lesson ('the sweep stopped at the surface the ticket named') applied pre-emptively. The split-fail-closed precedent to mirror is ADR 0013 section 3 (instance-resolution deny vs ancestor-collapse).

title: B2 supplier-outage: outage error-distinct from no-role at the RoleDefinitionSupplier SPI (design settled)
rationale: Grill-me 2026-06-15 settled the B2 phase-① design (ADR 0014 + B2-SUPPLIER-OUTAGE/00-DESIGN). The fix for the one widening-on-failure path (PERMISSION-CATEGORIES-REVIEW C1/C4, aggravated by 6.5): a TRI-STATE RoleDefinitionSupplier contract — Optional.of=resolved; Optional.empty()=authoritative no-role (KEEP, designed realm-fallback signal); THROW RoleResolutionException=outage (deny/no-widening). Pins: (1) unchecked RoleResolutionException in opa-abac-core (family-consistent w/ AncestorResolutionException; keeps @FunctionalInterface lambdas working); (2) STRICT HTTP invariant in HttpRoleDefinitionSupplier — ONLY 204->empty/fallback, ONLY 200+valid->resolved, EVERYTHING ELSE THROWS (200-blank, all 4xx, 5xx, timeout, refused, malformed-200); (3) supplier-classifies/consumer-maps, NO library wrapper (a wrapper either re-introduces the bug or is ceremony; 'deny' is non-uniform across consumers); (4) per-consumer mapping across ALL 5 lookup() consumers — gate managers (OpaPreAuthorize/OpaAuthorizationManager)->explicit catch->403 (the only widening path; rest have no fallback), HierarchicalAuthorizer->catch->false, SubtreeSpecResolver->NO CODE CHANGE (existing catch already collapses; test-only), CategoryListAuthorizer->catch->Page.empty(); (5) NO kill-switch (off-ramp would BE the vuln — consciously breaks the house pattern); (6) ZERO Rego — fallback clause RETAINED (load-bearing for non-members/type-level creates per 5.97); outage denies before any OPA call; opa test 157/157 unchanged; (7) TeamRoleDefinitionSupplier minimal touch (catch DataAccessException->throw, contract-conformant showcase; outcome unchanged, no fallback in user-mgmt); (8) logging WARN at supplier throw-site / DEBUG at consumer catches, no PII (uniform-403 means server log is the only operator outage signal); (9) resilience (retry/circuit-break) OUT of scope -> new Slice B3 (all cross-service HTTP edges: HttpRoleDefinitionSupplier+TagDefinitionClient+OpaClient), sequenced B2->6.7->Phase6->B3->Phase7. Headline proof: IT — realm catalog-editor + mock-supplier-throws (outage) + id'd write the resolved role narrows -> 403 NOT widened fallback (the C1/C4 cut). Ready for /decompose.

name: B2 decomposition package: 5 tickets, the all-5-consumer sweep as the discipline
description: B2 (supplier-outage) decomposed into 5 tickets (docs/to-do/planning/B2-SUPPLIER-OUTAGE). Critical path T1 -> {T2,T3,T4} -> T5; T1+T2 the independently-landable subset (the library spine carrying the ONLY widening path). T1 core (RoleResolutionException + tri-state SPI javadoc, additive, Spring-free). T2 spring-security (the behavioral fix: explicit catch RoleResolutionException -> DENY in BOTH gate managers, before the existing broad catch-all; sibling test proves Optional.empty()->fallback unbroken). T3 spring-data (HierarchicalAuthorizer catch->false; SubtreeSpecResolver NO CODE CHANGE -> test-only proof its existing catch(RuntimeException) collapses the throw). T4 example (HttpRoleDefinitionSupplier strict classification: only 204->empty, only 200+valid->resolved, ALL else throws; CategoryListAuthorizer wrap->Page.empty; TeamRoleDefinitionSupplier catch DataAccessException->throw, conformant showcase; Demo javadoc). T5 e2e+headline IT (SupplierOutageGateIT: realm catalog-editor + supplier-throws -> 403 handler-never-ran; contrast 204->fallback grants) + whole-suite green (opa test 157/157 unchanged) + docs reconcile (PERMISSION-MODEL, ABAC-AUTHORIZATION). KEYSTONE DISCIPLINE baked into the decomposition + the prompt's hard rules + the ★ gate: this slice exists BECAUSE the PERMISSION-CATEGORIES review found 'the sweep stopped at the surface the ticket named' -> all 5 lookup() consumers are explicit tickets, a throw with no consumer test is an unfinished sweep. Pinned semantics in 01-DECOMPOSITION so the run never stops: outage->uniform 403 (no 503/kill-switch/error-code); strict 204-only HTTP invariant. Verify gate: PACKAGE OK. Ready for the autonomous run on feature/void3110/supplier-outage.

name: Tri-state RoleDefinitionSupplier: outage throws, no-role is empty, each consumer maps to its own fail-closed
description: B2 closes the one widening-on-failure path: RoleDefinitionSupplier.lookup() became TRI-STATE so a role-source OUTAGE can't be mistaken for an authoritative NO-ROLE. Optional.of=resolved; Optional.empty()=authoritative no-role (a DESIGNED signal — the policy may fall back to realm roles, RETAINED); throw RoleResolutionException=outage (source unavailable, result UNKNOWN -> caller MUST fail closed, never fall back). RoleResolutionException is a new unchecked RuntimeException in opa-abac-core (Spring-free; mirrors AncestorResolutionException but a SEPARATE failure axis — never conflate role-source-outage with ancestor-chain-collapse). Mechanism: the SUPPLIER classifies (throws on outage) — the one place classification lives — and EACH consumer CATCHES and maps the throw to its OWN fail-closed outcome. NO library wrapper: a wrapper that caught->empty would re-introduce the exact bug, and 'deny' is not uniform across consumers (403 at a gate vs empty-page vs no-subtree-widening). The safety discipline is the explicit contract + a mandatory per-consumer outage test cell, not a runtime transform. Pinned in ADR 0014.

name: Strict HTTP role-source classification: only 204->empty, only 200+valid->resolved, everything else throws
description: The B2 HttpRoleDefinitionSupplier classification invariant (ADR 0014 section 4): stop swallowing failures. ONLY 204 -> Optional.empty() (authoritative no-role -> the policy realm fallback may decide). ONLY 200+non-blank+parseable body -> Optional.of(resolved). EVERYTHING ELSE THROWS RoleResolutionException (outage -> deny): 200-blank (a contract-violating 200 is untrustworthy, not no-role), ALL 4xx (the resolve protocol is not working as designed — never the designed 204), ALL 5xx, timeout, connection-refused/IOException, malformed-200 (Jackson parse failure). Treating any non-204 as no-role lets a misrouted/misconfigured/corrupt response silently WIDEN via the realm fallback — the whole bug. Impl notes: use NARROW catches (IOException / InterruptedException / JacksonException), NOT a broad catch(Exception), so a programming bug (e.g. NPE) is not mislabeled as an outage; restore the interrupt flag on InterruptedException before throwing; WARN with status-code or exception-class ONLY — never the userId/token/body (assert this with a no-PII test). Resilience (retry/backoff) is a SEPARATE axis -> Slice B3, not here.

name: 5-consumer sweep for a RoleDefinitionSupplier SPI change: gate x2 + hierarchy + subtree + list
description: An SPI-contract change to RoleDefinitionSupplier.lookup() must sweep ALL FIVE production consumers, not just the one the ticket names (the review lesson 'the sweep stopped at the surface the ticket named', PERMISSION-CATEGORIES-REVIEW). The five, with their B2 outage mapping: (1) OpaPreAuthorizeAuthorizationManager -> explicit catch(RoleResolutionException) -> DENY before the broad catch(Exception); (2) OpaAuthorizationManager -> same; both are the ONLY consumers with a realm fallback, so they carry the only widening path — the outage must deny BEFORE any OpaClient call so the fallback is never fed an outage input (assert verify(opaClient, never()).allow). (3) HierarchicalAuthorizer -> catch around the governing-root lookup -> return false (no fallback in this seam; needed a new catch + a logger field, the throw previously ESCAPED uncaught). (4) SubtreeSpecResolver -> NO CODE CHANGE (its existing catch(RuntimeException)->Optional.empty() already collapses it) but ADD a test pinning the SPECIFIC RoleResolutionException type so a refactor can't silently widen. (5) CategoryListAuthorizer (example) -> catch -> Page.empty(pageable) (the direct lookup escaped -> would be a 500; the SubtreeSpecResolver path it also calls is already fail-closed). Plus 4 implementors: NoOp/Demo never throw (in-process -> additivity), Http classifies (the fix), Team* minimal touch (DataAccessException->throw). A throw with NO consumer test = an unfinished sweep.

title: 6.7 control-plane categorization: CONTROL category + two-axis separation (verb vs escalation gate)
rationale: Phase 6.7 phase-① grill-me (2026-06-15) settled the control-plane vocabulary shape. ONE shared category vocabulary (not a separate control-plane taxonomy): team:* verbs fold into permission_categories.json. The full split of the coarse 'manage' verb into membership fine-actions makes CONTROL a REFINABLE category (the catalog's WRITE pattern). GROUPING: READ -> [view, list, list-members] (any team member can now list the roster — an externally-visible behavior change from today's manager-only listing); CONTROL -> [add-member, change-role, remove-member] (membership mutation, deny-refinable: deny remove-member = onboard/retitle but never remove). define-tags STAYS under TAG (already in the table). define-roles + transfer-ownership remain OWNER-ONLY FENCES outside the category system (ADR 0007's escalation-via-authoring branch stays pruned). THE 6.7 PRINCIPLE — two orthogonal axes: (1) the VERB category (CONTROL + deny-overrides) decides WHICH KINDS of membership acts a role may perform; (2) the SHIPPED escalation gates in MembershipService (cross-tier strict <, senior subset-on-effective, target-tier, owner-protection) decide ON WHOM and TO WHAT TIER. 6.7 touches ONLY axis 1; axis 2 is an invariant, untouched. Consequence: holding add-member does NOT imply change-role (independent fine actions); and whatever verbs you hold, the gates still forbid acting on anyone above your tier or promoting past your own ceiling. Single-expansion-home teaching artifact preserved: team.rego will call effective_actions(role_def, 'team') exactly like catalog.rego.

title: 6.7 resolve-side: team management ladder stays a Java projection (TeamRoleCapabilities recast to category tokens), custom roles management-incapable
rationale: 6.7 phase-① (2026-06-15). DISCOVERY: seeded system roles store category tokens under the WILDCARD '*' key ({owner/admin: [READ,WRITE,TAG,GRANT]}, senior/member: [READ,WRITE,TAG], reader: [READ]) — these are RESOURCE perms (resourceRole expands '*' -> target type). The TEAM MANAGEMENT ladder is a SEPARATE, narrower, code-driven projection (admin's mgmt = read/manage/define-tags, NOT its resource GRANT) synthesized by TeamRoleCapabilities.forCode — it CANNOT be read from the stored '*' tokens because the two sets deliberately differ (owner's define-roles/transfer-ownership have no resource analog). So the mgmt ladder stays a JAVA PROJECTION, recast from fine verbs to CATEGORY TOKENS: owner/administrator -> [READ, CONTROL, TAG]; senior -> [READ, CONTROL]; member/reader -> [READ]; custom code -> [READ] (the I12 fence). managementRole keeps shape Map.of('team', forCode(code)); team.rego expands those tokens via the SHARED data.permission_categories (single expansion home, symmetric with catalog.rego). Owner-only fences (define-roles, transfer-ownership) are NOT in the token map — enforced by team.rego's owner-by-code rule. CUSTOM ROLES stay management-incapable (Option A, I12 'ceiling != capability' preserved): managementRole projects custom codes to READ-only on type:team regardless of stored permissions; validateContract TIGHTENED to reject CONTROL (and team-meaningful TAG) tokens under the 'team' key for custom roles — turning today's silent dead-data into an explicit 422. Rejected moving the ladder into OPA data (would create a 2nd table, break single-expansion-home). Rejected opening custom-role team power (separate bigger escalation analysis, would bloat the slice).

title: 6.7 OPA wiring: mirror permissions.rego + permission_categories.json into the user-mgmt service bundle; keep TAG intact, add CONTROL only
rationale: 6.7 phase-① (2026-06-15). TWO OPA bundles: runtime = single shared OPA container mounting infra/opa/policies/ (has team.rego + permissions.rego + permission_categories.json + role.rego + catalog policies — all co-loaded, so team.rego CAN reference data.permissions.effective_actions at runtime today). But example-user-management-service/src/main/resources/opa/policies/ is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for team.rego and holds ONLY team.rego + team_test.rego — its isolated 'opa test' (14/14) would BREAK once team.rego calls data.permissions.effective_actions. DECISION (Option A): copy permissions.rego + permission_categories.json VERBATIM into the service bundle so the dogfood team.rego resolves effective_actions and opa test stays self-contained per-module. Consistent with the already-accepted duplication model (README: service bundle = source of truth, infra = a mounted copy). PROOF OBLIGATION / two-copy gotcha to pin for the run: the CONTROL category + the list-members addition to READ must land in BOTH permission_categories.json copies (infra + service); permissions.rego copied verbatim. FINAL 6.7 CATEGORY TABLE: READ->[view,list,list-members]; WRITE->[create,update,delete] (unchanged); TAG->[define-tags,assign-tags] (UNCHANGED — define-tags stays in TAG, kept there to avoid a 2nd new category + shipped-catalog churn; per-plane inertness is intentional: define-tags live only on team, assign-tags only on catalog); GRANT->[assign-roles] (unchanged); CONTROL->[add-member,change-role,remove-member] (the ONE new category). define-tags re-gating is purely mechanical: team:define-tags annotation unchanged, now granted via the TAG token in owner/admin ladder + expanded by team.rego; behavior identical (owner/admin curate, others 403); senior correctly stays WITHOUT define-tags (holds CONTROL not TAG).

title: 6.7 proof obligations + behavior delta: counts RISE (not zero-Rego like B2), list-members loosening + custom-role 422 are the two intended behavior changes
rationale: 6.7 phase-① (2026-06-15) close-out. BASELINE: opa test infra 157, service-team 14. EXPECTED DELTA (pinned as direction+which-tests-change, NOT a magic number — decompose ② sets exact targets): infra RISES (~+8-12), service-team RISES (~20+). KNOWN INTENDED BREAK (the one a run could misread as regression): permissions_test.rego asserts READ=={view,list} at ~3 sites (lines 11-12,29-31,78) — these MUST update to {view,list,list-members}. ADD CONTROL expansion cases to permissions_test.rego. team_test.rego (BOTH copies) rewritten to the category model: every system code x every control verb, owner-only fence (define-roles/transfer-ownership allowed ONLY for code=='owner'), define-tags via TAG for owner/admin but NOT senior, unknown-token-denies, no-role-def-denies. MIRROR OBLIGATION: both permission_categories.json copies byte-identical after edit. TWO INTENDED EXTERNALLY-VISIBLE BEHAVIOR CHANGES (everything else is net-identical authorization, only wire-verb renames manage->add-member/change-role/remove-member): (1) list-members moves team:manage->READ so ANY team member can list the roster (today manager-only) — proof: member CAN GET /members AND member/reader still 403 on mutations+define-tags (loosening is EXACTLY listing); add a newman cell for it too. (2) validateContract now 422s a custom role carrying CONTROL/team-meaningful-TAG tokens under a 'team' key (was silent dead-data). NO DB/Liquibase migration — team ladder is a pure Java projection; system-role '*' resource seeds untouched. B2 tri-state supplier contract is a NON-GOAL (untouched). AUTONOMOUS-RUN RISK PINS (recurring planning-gap classes): the unpinned-fail-open-semantic class is covered by enumerating the full behavior delta above; the rig/two-copy gotcha class is covered by the mirror-both-bundles + both-team.rego-copies obligations + 'restart OPA after editing team.rego' (README) for any live e2e.

name: Category-driven team.rego: two-rule allow (effective_actions + owner-only-by-code fence) mirrored byte-for-byte across both bundles
description: Phase 6.7 made the control plane category-driven, symmetric with catalog.rego. team.rego's allow is TWO rules: (1) category-driven — guard on input.role_definition.permissions, then 'verb in permissions.effective_actions(input.role_definition, input.resource.type)' (the SAME shared expansion home the catalog uses; import data.permissions); (2) an owner-only FENCE — 'verb in {"define-roles","transfer-ownership"}' AND 'input.role_definition.code == "owner"'. The fence is keyed on the reserved owner CODE, never role_level — verified by opa eval: a custom level-40 role carrying CONTROL still gets transfer-ownership=false. Mirror obligation: team.rego + team_test.rego + permission_categories.json + permissions.rego must be BYTE-IDENTICAL in both bundles (infra/opa/policies + the user-mgmt service bundle); permissions.rego/the table are copied verbatim into the service bundle ONLY so its isolated opa test resolves data.permissions (runtime co-loads from the shared infra bundle). Test-maintenance gotcha when WIDENING a category (READ gained list-members): EVERY assertion that expands that category rises (8 sites for READ), AND any 'deny everything granted -> set()' test must add the new fine action to its denied_actions or it stops being empty. opa test counts: infra 157->177, service-team 14->30.

name: Custom-role management-incapability is defended by TWO independent fences + a JSON-parity drift guard
description: Phase 6.7 keeps custom roles management-incapable with two fences that don't depend on each other: (1) the PROJECTION — EffectiveRoleService.managementRole calls TeamRoleCapabilities.forCode(code), which returns [READ] for ANY non-system code regardless of what the row stores, so a custom role's stored team tokens can never reach the dogfooded policy; (2) AUTHORING VALIDATION — RoleDefinitionService.validateContract now 422s a custom role carrying CONTROL under any key, or CONTROL/TAG under a 'team' key (TAG-under-team would grant define-tags). READ-under-team stays valid (the harmless list-members loosening). Either fence alone suffices; both is defense-in-depth. Vocabulary ownership: 'which categories are authorable vs control-plane' lives in PermissionCategories (CONTROL_PLANE_CATEGORIES={CONTROL}, AUTHORABLE_CATEGORIES={READ,WRITE,TAG,GRANT}), NOT as a literal in the service. DRIFT GUARD: PermissionCategoriesParityTest pins PermissionCategories.EXPANSION byte-for-byte to permission_categories.json (U9) AND asserts the authorable/control-plane sets partition the full vocabulary with no ceiling holding a control-plane category — so adding a category to the JSON without updating the Java sets breaks the build. When widening the table (T1), the Java EXPANSION + these sets must move in lockstep or U9 goes red.

After splitting team:manage into fine verbs (T3) and recasting TeamRoleCapabilities to category tokens (T2), every user-mgmt membership/tag/transfer IT went red — NOT because the app was wrong, but because AbacTestConfig.inProcessTeamOpaClient() is an in-process Java MIRROR of team.rego (the ITs run WITHOUT an OPA container; the secured chain calls this stub for the dogfooded @OpaPreAuthorize gate). The mirror still did the OLD raw match granted.contains(verb), so once managementRole emitted [READ,CONTROL,TAG] it denied every now-fine verb (add-member not literally in the token list). Also one IT (viewerCannotManage) encoded the OLD contract (reader GET /members -> 403) that 6.7 intentionally loosens to 200 (list-members in READ) — a known intended break, like the permissions_test READ-expansion break.
resolution: Any slice that changes team.rego's decision shape MUST update AbacTestConfig.inProcessTeamOpaClient() in lockstep (it's a parallel implementation of the policy for the no-container IT path) — and grep the existing ITs for cells that assert the OLD allow/deny contract. Recast the mirror to expand category tokens through PermissionCategories.EXPANSION (the U9-parity-pinned table — reuse it so IT math can't drift from the OPA data file) minus denied_actions, plus the owner-only-by-code fence (verb in {define-roles,transfer-ownership} AND code=="owner"). This is a build-breaker that lands in the SAME ticket as the verb split, not deferred. The two-axis MembershipGateIT escalation cells pass UNCHANGED through the renamed verbs (the gates are orthogonal).

name: Live-rig e2e after a team.rego/projection change: restart OPA + rebuild the usermgmt image + recreate the pod, then grep the e2e for OLD-contract cells
description: Running the e2e after a 6.7-style control-plane change needs THREE rig steps, in order: (1) restart OPA (docker restart opa-abac-opa) so it reloads the edited team.rego + permission_categories.json from the ./opa/policies mount (--watch unreliable) — verify with curl localhost:28181/v1/data/permission_categories + opa eval probes; (2) rebuild the usermgmt image with the NEW Java (docker build -q -t opa-abac-usermgmt:local -f example-user-management-service/Dockerfile . — a full Gradle-in-container build, slow); (3) recreate the pod: docker compose -p opa-abac-example -f infra/compose.usermgmt.yaml up -d --force-recreate usermgmt, then wait for localhost:28090/actuator/health. The CATALOG image does NOT need rebuilding (no catalog code changed; catalog cells decide via the shared OPA). Intended-break sweep: the existing e2e matrices encode the OLD contract — team-abac cell 8 ('viewer GET /members -> 403') and the permission-categories cells assert pre-6.7 outcomes; the list-members loosening flips viewer/member GET /members to 200, so REWRITE those cells (viewer lists 200 / mutates 403) and ADD explicit loosening cells. Add new cells via a Python json edit reusing the runner's existing --env-var tokens (senior_token/ladder_token/team_id/target1_uid). Result: permission-categories 31/31, team 12/12, all other matrices unaffected (list-members inert on catalog) -> 129 assertions across 10 matrices, 0 failed.

When a slice ADDS a file to a mirrored bundle, the existing drift guard does not automatically cover it. 6.7 made team.rego category-driven, so the user-mgmt service bundle gained verbatim copies of permissions.rego + permission_categories.json (the mirror obligation). But the CI 'must not drift' step in .github/workflows/ci.yml diffed only the PRE-EXISTING two files (team.rego + team_test.rego), and the U9 PermissionCategoriesParityTest pinned the Java EXPANSION to the INFRA json only (never read the service-bundle copy). So the two NEW mirror files could drift from infra silently — diff was clean at ship time, but nothing enforced it.
